post.summary:
Assigns one Expert design template to several elements in a single call, or detaches them from the
template they currently carry. Only the design template of each element is changed - every other
property is left exactly as it is, which is what makes this different from UpdateElement.



A template is applied to an element only when all three conditions hold: it is a template of the
same KIND of element, of the same MATERIAL FAMILY as the element, and it carries the property set
of the DESIGN CODE the model is configured with at the moment of the call. Elements that break a
rule are reported individually in the diagnostics and are left untouched; the rest are still
applied, and the returned value is true only when every requested element was assigned.

post.summary: Writes one group of the general settings of the model.
post.description:
There is no category parameter: the `$type` of the body says which group is
written and in which shape, so adding a group of settings adds no action here.



Partial by design - every group and every property is optional, and what is not sent
keeps the value the model has. A property the model derives from another one cannot be
imposed: such a value is ignored and reported as a warning, not refused, so that an
object just read can be handed straight back.



For `CombinationsGeneration`: call it before `GenerateCombinations`, which is
the only thing that reads those settings, and send the shape matching the standard the
model generates for, which `GetModelSettings` reports.

requestBody.description: The settings to write, as an instance of the class of the group concerned.

schema.description:
Base class of the GENERAL SETTINGS of a model: the options that apply to the model as a
whole rather than to any one object of it, and that in the AD model live on
`som.ModelProperties`.



These are NOT properties of an element, a load case or a combination. They are what the
desktop application edits in its option dialogs - which project situations the combination
generation produces, which coefficients it applies, and, as they are added, the general
options of the Expert design calculations. They are read, written and reset through THREE
generic functions, whatever the group:

- `GetModelSettings(category)` returns the settings of one group,

- `SetModelSettings(settings)` writes them, and

- `ResetModelSettings(category)` puts back what the model's standard prescribes.



THE OBJECT DECIDES WHAT IS WRITTEN. `SetModelSettings` takes this base class, so it is
the runtime type of the object - its `$type` - that says which group of model settings
the call writes, exactly as `CreateInformationalElement` takes
AD.API.InformationalElementBase and the object decides what is created. There is no
function per group of settings, and adding a group adds no function.



TWO LEVELS OF DERIVATION. Under this base, one class per group of settings
(AD.API.CombinationsGenerationSettings, AD.API.SteelCalculationSettings and
AD.API.AiscSteelCalculationSettings today) - and under that class, as many classes as
the group has shapes. The combination generation has five, one per combination standard,
because the standards share no field; each of the two steel groups has one, because the
codes inside a family share every page of the dialog. So the class hierarchy reads: what
settings (level 2), in which variant (level 3).



TWO STEEL GROUPS, NOT ONE GROUP WITH TWO SHAPES. The Eurocode and the North-American
families do not answer the same question - the second has no Partial safety factors page at
all and a Verification page of three controls instead of thirteen - so they are separate
categories with separate group classes. The five pages they do share are the same DTO
classes, held by both group classes.



PARTIAL BY DESIGN. In every group, the properties are optional and what a request does not
carry keeps the value the model has, so a single switch can be changed without restating
the rest. What each group refuses, what it recomputes rather than stores, and what it
reports as a warning instead of an error is documented on that group's own class.

post.summary: launch the calculation of the model

Launches the Expert design calculation of one material family on the model.



The FEM analysis MUST have been run before (LaunchAnalysis): the design engines verify design
criteria against the finite element results, so the call fails with an explicit diagnostic when
the model was never calculated. The design code (EC2/EC3/EC5/EC4, AISC, CM66, BS, ACI, CSA, ...)
and the kind of each element are not parameters - the design modules decide them from the code
configured on the model and from what each element actually is.



Everything the design engine reports while it calculates is returned in the response
diagnostics, so a partially successful calculation can be diagnosed element by element.

parameters.name: designType
parameters.description: The material family whose design engine is launched.

schema.description:
Material family whose Expert design engine is launched by LaunchDesignCalculation

Possible values:

  • 0 - Concrete: Reinforced concrete design (called "BA" - beton arme - in the AD model): EC2, BAEL, ACI, BS 8110 or STAS, depending on the concrete design code configured on the model.
  • 1 - Steel: Steelwork design: EC3 (1st or 2nd generation), CM66, AISC or CSA, depending on the steel design code configured on the model.
  • 2 - Timber: Timber design: EC5 or the North-American codes (O86 / NDS), depending on the timber design code configured on the model.
  • 3 - Composite: Composite beam (steel section + concrete slab) design: EC4, AISC 360 or CSA S16, depending on the composite design code configured on the model.

requestBody.description:
Optional. The internal IDs of the elements to calculate; null or an empty list calculates every
element of the model. Ignored for Composite, whose engine reads its own element set from the
model (a warning is added to the diagnostics in that case).

post.summary: Get the results a Design Expert produced for the elements named by the query.
post.description:
Not to be confused with M:AD.API.Srv.Controllers.ModelController.GetResults(AD.API.ResultType,System.Collections.Generic.List{System.Int64},System.Int64), which returns finite element results for one
load case. These are design-code verification results: the engine already checked every
combination and kept the most unfavourable one, whose index each result reports, so the query
names no load case. The design must have been calculated first with
`LaunchDesignCalculation`.
            
The payload is the polymorphic AD.API.ResultsQueryDesign base, so the same endpoint will
serve the concrete, timber and composite experts once those are exposed; the concrete type is
selected through the "$type" discriminator and today only
AD.API.ResultsQueryDesignSteelLinear is answered.
            
Note that the reasons a result is missing - the design was never run, the model uses a
non-Eurocode steel code, an element id is unknown or is not a linear element - are reported by
the engine as warnings, which are stripped from the response unless the session was opened with
`LogVerboseLevel.ErrorsAndWarnings`.

get.summary: Reads where the current model stands in the mesh -> finite element -> design chain.
get.description:
Whether an analysis model exists, the state of the mesh, whether the finite element
analysis was run and how many analysis cases carry results, which of the four design
experts have calculated, and how construction stages stand - plus a single
`OverallState` summarizing all of it.



A pure read, and a cheap one: every value is a flag or a counter the model already carries,
no element of the model is visited, and nothing is created, opened or calculated. Call it as
often as you like - before `LaunchAnalysis` to see there is nothing yet, after it to
check what was produced, after `LaunchDesignCalculation` to see which family ran.



One property must not be used as a freshness gate without reading its documentation:
`FemIsUpToDate` is maintained by the desktop application only, so in a headless session
it never reports that YOUR changes invalidated the results - and `OverallState` is
therefore never `OutOfDate` there.

requestBody.description: The environment settings for the project.

schema.description:
Environment settings - the language, the localization, the diagnostics verbosity and the
design standards a session runs under.



IT CONFIGURES THE SESSION, AND A SESSION IS CONFIGURED ONCE. The environment takes effect on
the `NewProject` / `OpenProject` call that opens the session and lasts as long as
that project. A call sent while a project is still open is REFUSED - the whole call, not
just the environment: the localization and design standards were read while that model was
built and are read again by the generation and by the design Experts, so running a second
project on them would calculate it under standards it was never described with. Close the
project first; the next one takes a new environment.



THE LANGUAGE IS NARROWER STILL - fixed for the life of the SERVER PROCESS. The first
environment settles it, and the two ways of changing it afterwards are treated differently:


* an EXPLICIT AD.API.Environments.Language that disagrees with the one in force is REFUSED, and
  the caller is told to restart the server;


* a language merely IMPLIED by AD.API.Environments.Localization is HELD BACK with a warning, and
  the rest of that localization - its eight design standards, which is what it is really
  being asked for - is applied normally. Refusing here instead would tie a whole server to
  one localization family, since sixteen of the eighteen localizations imply a language
  other than English.



The restriction is what the desktop application achieves by restarting itself: reloading the
prompt database is not enough, because the catalogues, units and resources already loaded
keep the language they were read in.



WHAT IT WRITES. Everything this environment configures lives in the server's memory for the
life of the session; no design standard, annex, localization or language chosen here is
written back to the machine's Advance Design configuration. One thing is not in that
promise, and it is not this API's doing: OPENING the in-memory session seeds it by reading
the per-user registry, and Advance Design's own accessors write a default back when they
find a value missing. So on a machine where Advance Design has never run, the first request
materialises the default keys - with the values the read already resolved to, never with
anything this request named.

environment settles it, and the two ways of changing it afterwards are treated differently:


* an EXPLICIT AD.API.Environments.Language that disagrees with the one in force is REFUSED, and
  the caller is told to restart the server;


* a language merely IMPLIED by AD.API.Environments.Localization is HELD BACK with a warning, and
  the rest of that localization - its eight design standards, which is what it is really
  being asked for - is applied normally. Refusing here instead would tie a whole server to
  one localization family, since sixteen of the eighteen localizations imply a language
  other than English.



The restriction is what the desktop application achieves by restarting itself: reloading the
prompt database is not enough, because the catalogues, units and resources already loaded
keep the language they were read in.



WHAT IT WRITES. Everything this environment configures lives in the server's memory for the
life of the session; no design standard, annex, localization or language chosen here is
written back to the machine's Advance Design configuration. One thing is not in that
promise, and it is not this API's doing: OPENING the in-memory session seeds it by reading
the per-user registry, and Advance Design's own accessors write a default back when they
find a value missing. So on a machine where Advance Design has never run, the first request
materialises the default keys - with the values the read already resolved to, never with
anything this request named.

get.summary:
Reads back the environment in force: the language, the localization, the log verbosity and
all sixteen design standards and national annexes.
get.description:
Every design standard and annex comes back set, whether it was named in the
`NewProject` / `OpenProject` request or resolved from the localization - this is
what the session HOLDS, not an echo of what was asked for. Use it to find out what a
localization resolves to, and to confirm what an override actually changed.

FAILS when no project is open, with `ENVIRONMENT_NO_SESSION`. The environment is a
property of the session and the session lasts exactly as long as the project, so outside one
there is nothing to report - and reading the engine's defaults anyway would both describe
the machine rather than this server and write those defaults into the per-user registry.
A standard the session carries but this API does not publish - a 2nd generation Eurocode,
CM66, BS 8110, all of which the desktop application can configure - comes back as
`null` for that one property, with a warning naming the property and the raw number.
It is not reported as a number: the generated clients renumber their copy of each
enumeration, so a number would be read back as a DIFFERENT standard.

post.summary: Saves the open project to its own file.
post.description:
`Data` is true and the diagnostics carry `PROJECT_SAVED` (information) when the project was saved.
            Otherwise `Data` is false with, as error: `PROJECT_NOT_OPEN` when no project is open,
            `PROJECT_SAVE_FAILED` when the engine could not save it (its own messages say why; the project stays open,
            as it was), `PROJECT_SAVE_EXCEPTION` for an internal error.

post.summary: Saves the open project to a new project file, which from then on is the session's project.
post.description:
The same Save As as Advance Design's (File > Save As): the model and the analysis model, the results, and the
documents, design and selected templates folders of the project are written to the new project, so that it
opens in Advance Design in the same state. The file opened before is left as it was at its last save. From this
call on the session works on the new file: `SaveProject` and `CloseProject` write to it.



As in Advance Design, the spaces around the name and before the extension are dropped, a name holding the
extension twice is refused, and the path must stay 28 characters shorter than the Windows path limit (260).



Refused, before anything is written: `PROJECT_NOT_OPEN` when no project is open,
`PROJECT_INVALID_FILENAME` / `PROJECT_INVALID_EXTENSION` as for `NewProject` (and for the extension
twice),
`PROJECT_FOLDER_NOT_FOUND` when the folder that is to contain the file does not exist (it is not created),
`PROJECT_TARGET_EXISTS` when the file or its project folder (the file's path without `.fto`) already
exists - saving there would first empty it -, and `PROJECT_TARGET_INVALID` when the new project folder and
the open project's folder would lie one inside the other.


`Data` is true and the diagnostics carry `PROJECT_SAVED_AS` (information) when the project was saved to
the new file. Otherwise `Data` is false with `PROJECT_SAVE_AS_FAILED` (or `PROJECT_SAVE_AS_EXCEPTION`
for an internal error), whose message says which project the session is on:
<list type="bullet"><item>"The session's project is still ..." - nothing was written. It is so for the refusals the engine side makes
before writing: a path longer than the limit above, a folder that cannot be written to. The open project is
unchanged and can still be saved and closed as usual.</item><item>"The session's project is now ..." - the engine had begun: the session is on the new, possibly partial,
copy. Do NOT save it (no `SaveProject`, no `CloseProject`): close it with `CloseProjectWithoutSave`,
check both folders, and open the original again.</item></list>

parameters.name: filename

post.summary: Saves the open project, then closes it.
post.description: To close it without saving, call `CloseProjectWithoutSave`.

post.summary: Closes the open project WITHOUT saving it: what changed since its last save is discarded.
post.description:
"Its last save": `SaveProject`, `SaveProjectAs`, and the operations that save the project on their
own - the calculations, the combinations generation, the model settings and the deletion of a structural system.
To save the project before closing it, call `CloseProject`.

post.summary: Close the current session and request the local API host to shut down.
post.description:
Use this endpoint when multiple automation sessions run in parallel and you want to release
the resources associated with the current one.



The call returns at once; the shutdown follows in the background, about 5 seconds later. The
server then waits for an operation or analysis that is already running (or queued) to finish,
saves and closes the open project - there is no need to call `CloseProject` first -
releases the licence, and the process exits. How long that takes depends on the operation still
running and on the size of the project. To close the open project without saving it, call
`CloseSessionWithoutSave` instead.



From this call on, every other `api/Model` request is refused at once with HTTP 503 and the
error code `SERVICE_STOPPING`, and `GET api/Service/GetStatus` answers `Stopping`
until the process has exited. Calling `CloseSession` again is harmless: the first close requested decides how
the project is closed, and the `SESSION_CLOSING` message of a later call says it joined that close and
what it does.

post.summary: Close the current session WITHOUT saving the open project, and request the local API host to shut down.
post.description:
The same as `CloseSession`, except that a project still open is closed without saving: what changed since
its last save is discarded, as with `CloseProjectWithoutSave`.



The first close requested decides how the project is closed: a `CloseSession` or
`CloseSessionWithoutSave` called afterwards - or a stop of the host (Ctrl+C) - joins the close already
requested and changes nothing. The `SESSION_CLOSING` message always says what the close in force does:
a call that joined an earlier `CloseSession` (or a stop of the host) reports that the project is saved.

get.summary: Returns the version of the Advance Design API service.
get.description: Doubles as a liveness probe ("ping"): it needs no project and no model, it never blocks, and an HTTP 200 carrying a version string proves the service is up and answering.

get.summary:
Returns whether the Advance Design API service can run model operations, and if not, why -
today: whether it holds its licence, and what that licence allows.
get.description:
Needs no project and no model, and is not queued behind a running model operation or analysis: the licence part is a snapshot taken when the service started and refreshed now and then while the service is idle (`licence.checkedAt` says when).



Always HTTP 200 while the service answers: the verdict is in the body. Decide with `canRun`; `status` is a string that may take new values in later versions - treat any value other than `Ok` as "not Ok". While the service is still starting, the call waits up to 30 seconds and may answer `Starting`: ask again.

AD_API_ActionType.description:
Action type

Possible values:

  • 0 - ClimaticAutoGeneration: auto climatic generation for existing climatic(wind and snow) load case families

sectionClass.description:
Cross-section class (maps to "SectionClass"). 

Displayed as "Cross section class". 

AISC classifies a section as compact, noncompact or slender-element, so this property is typed
with AD.API.SteelSectionClassAISC and NOT with the
AD.API.SteelSectionClass used by the Eurocode and CAN/CSA leaves - the same stored
integer, read against a different list. 

Unlike the two other codes, AISC has no imposed effective (Class 4) characteristics: there is
nothing for the class to enable. 

Default value : SteelSectionClassAISC.auto_class

AISCSteelLinearDesignTemplate.description:
Expert design template for linear STEEL elements verified to AISC 360 (maps to the AD model
object `som.AISCSteelLinearRole`, held by `som.Role` in its
"AISCSteelLinearExpertProperties" slot). 


It corresponds to the "Design template description" dialog of Advance Design when the material
is Steel, the element type is Linear and the model's steel design code is an AISC one. 


The template name is the base-class member AD.API.InformationalElementBase.UserName; it
must be unique among the steel/linear templates of the model and is limited to 50
characters. 


USED BY WHICH DESIGN CODES - this property set is the one Advance Design allocates for
AD.API.SteelDesignCode.aisc and AD.API.SteelDesignCode.aisc_2016. Both editions
share ONE class because they share one SOM object: `CRoleManager::AddRole` normalizes them
to a single "AISC" expert set, and neither the model nor the property list distinguishes them.
Creating this template in a model configured for any other steel code is refused, because the
engine would never allocate the AISC property set for it; the response diagnostics then name the
active code. 


PROPAGATION - assigning the template to a linear element, or editing the template afterwards,
copies these properties onto the element's own expert properties through the same mechanism the
user interface uses. Editing a template therefore changes every element that references it. 


PARTIAL UPDATE - every group of AD.API.NorthAmericanSteelLinearDesignTemplate is
nullable. On Update, a group left null keeps its stored value. 

Available for the descriptive model only.

AiscClassLoadingPattern.description:
Stress pattern a North American cross-section classification was performed against

Possible values:

  • 0 - AxialForce: Uniform axial force - the section classified for compression (or tension, where the code classifies it). Native suffix: _FX, from the engine's RES_NZ slot.
  • 1 - BendingYY: Bending about the y-y axis. Native suffix: _MY, from the engine's RES_MX slot.
  • 2 - BendingZZ: Bending about the z-z axis. Native suffix: _MZ, from the engine's RES_MY slot.
  • 3 - CombinedForces: The combined-forces stress pattern, classified for the interaction check. Native suffix: _FM, from the engine's RES_FM slot.

AiscCrossSectionClass.description:
AISC 360 section B4 cross-section classification. AISC 360 models only

Possible values:

  • 0 - Auto: No class determined. Native: aisc_CLASS_AUTO. Two different situations produce it: the engine was left to classify and has not done so yet, and - because of the memset above - a part slot that was never written.
  • 1 - Compact: Compact - the section can develop its full plastic moment and has the rotation capacity for plastic analysis. AISC 360 table B4.1, lambda below lambda-p. Native: aisc_CLASS_COMPACT / CLASS_COMPACT_AISC.
  • 2 - NonCompact: Non-compact - the extreme fibre can reach yield, but local buckling prevents the plastic moment from developing. lambda between lambda-p and lambda-r. Native: aisc_CLASS_NONCOMPACT / CLASS_NONCOMPACT_AISC.
  • 3 - SlenderElement: Slender-element - local buckling occurs before yield, so the reduced provisions of section E7 (for compression) or F5 (for flexure) apply. lambda above lambda-r. Native: aisc_CLASS_SLENDER_ELEMENT / CLASS_SLENDER_ELEMENT_AISC.
  • 4 - Unknown: The class could not be determined - the engine reports it for a shape it cannot classify, and turns it into

AiscDesignMethod.description:
Whether the reported strengths are ASD allowable or LRFD design values

Possible values:

  • 0 - Unknown: Not recorded. The native macros start at 1, so 0 cannot come out of a calculated result; it is here so that a file written by a future engine that leaves the field zeroed does not have to be reported as ASD.
  • 1 - ASD: Allowable Strength Design. Strength is Rn / Omega. Native: METHOD_ASD.
  • 2 - LRFD: Load and Resistance Factor Design. Strength is phi * Rn. Native: METHOD_LRFD. Also what a CSA S16 result reports, that code having no alternative format.

AiscFormula.description:
The AISC 360 equation a resistance check applied. AISC 360 models only

Possible values:

  • 0 - None: No equation recorded. Native: FORMULA_NONE.
  • 1 - D2_1: Equation (D2-1) - tensile yielding on the gross section. Native: FORMULA_D2_1.
  • 2 - E3_1: Equation (E3-1) - flexural buckling of a member without slender elements. Native: FORMULA_E3_1.
  • 3 - E4_1: Equation (E4-1) - torsional and flexural-torsional buckling. Native: FORMULA_E4_1.
  • 4 - E7_1: Equation (E7-1) - compressive strength of a member WITH slender elements. Native: FORMULA_E7_1.
  • 5 - F2: Section F2 - doubly symmetric compact I-shapes and channels bent about their major axis. Native: FORMULA_F2.
  • 6 - F3: Section F3 - doubly symmetric I-shapes with non-compact or slender flanges, major axis. Native: FORMULA_F3.
  • 7 - F4: Section F4 - other I-shapes with compact or non-compact webs, major axis. Native: FORMULA_F4.
  • 8 - F5: Section F5 - doubly and singly symmetric I-shapes with slender webs, major axis. Native: FORMULA_F5.
  • 9 - F6: Section F6 - I-shapes and channels bent about their minor axis. Native: FORMULA_F6.
  • 10 - F7: Section F7 - square and rectangular HSS, and box sections. Native: FORMULA_F7.
  • 11 - F8: Section F8 - round HSS. Native: FORMULA_F8.
  • 12 - F9: Section F9 - tees and double angles loaded in the plane of symmetry. Native: FORMULA_F9.
  • 13 - F10: Section F10 - single angles. Native: FORMULA_F10.
  • 14 - F11: Section F11 - rectangular bars and rounds. Native: FORMULA_F11.
  • 15 - F12: Section F12 - unsymmetrical shapes. Native: FORMULA_F12.
  • 16 - G2_1: Equation (G2-1) - shear strength of webs with or without transverse stiffeners. Native: FORMULA_G2_1.
  • 17 - G6_1: Equation (G6-1) - shear strength of round HSS. Native: FORMULA_G6_1.
  • 18 - H1_1A: Equation (H1-1a) - combined axial force and flexure, the branch used when the axial utilisation is at least 0.2. Native: FORMULA_H1_1A.
  • 19 - H1_1B: Equation (H1-1b) - combined axial force and flexure, the branch used below an axial utilisation of 0.2. Native: FORMULA_H1_1B.
  • 20 - H1_2: Equation (H1-2) - the alternative interaction for doubly symmetric rolled members in single-axis flexure and compression, which is why the block reports Pcy and McLTB. Native: FORMULA_H1_2.
  • 21 - H3_1: Equation (H3-1) - round HSS under torsion and combined stress. Native: FORMULA_H3_1.
  • 22 - H3_6: Equation (H3-6) - non-HSS members under torsion combined with other forces. Native: FORMULA_H3_6.
  • 23 - H2_1: Equation (H2-1) - unsymmetric members and members under combined stress, checked at a point. Native: FORMULA_H2_1.
  • 24 - H3_7: Equation (H3-7). Native: FORMULA_H3_7.
  • 25 - H3_8: Equation (H3-8). Native: FORMULA_H3_8.
  • 26 - H3_9: Equation (H3-9). Native: FORMULA_H3_9.
  • 27 - G3_1: Equation (G3-1) - tension field action. AISC 360-16 and later only. Native: FORMULA_G3_1.
  • 28 - G4_1: Equation (G4-1) - shear strength of single angles and tees. AISC 360-16 and later only. Native: FORMULA_G4_1.
  • 29 - G5_1: Equation (G5-1) - shear strength of rectangular HSS and box sections. AISC 360-16 and later only. Native: FORMULA_G5_1.
  • 30 - C_I3_10: Commentary equation (C-I3-10) - flexural strength of a composite beam. Native: FORMULA_C_I3_10.
  • 31 - C_I3_13: Commentary equation (C-I3-13) - flexural strength of a composite beam. Native: FORMULA_C_I3_13.

AiscResistanceCheckId.description:
Which check one entry of a North American cross-section resistance result describes

Possible values:

  • 0 - Axial: Axial force - tension (AISC 360 chapter D, CSA S16 clause 13.2) or compression (chapter E, clause 13.3).
  • 1 - ShearY: Shear along the y-y axis (AISC 360 chapter G, CSA S16 clause 13.4.1.1). Native suffix: Fy.
  • 2 - ShearZ: Shear along the z-z axis. Native suffix: Fz.
  • 3 - BendingYY: Bending about the y-y axis (AISC 360 chapter F, CSA S16 clauses 13.5 and 13.6). Native suffix: My, fed from the engine's RES_MX slot.
  • 4 - BendingZZ: Bending about the z-z axis. Native suffix: Mz, fed from the engine's RES_MY slot.
  • 5 - Torsion: Torsion (AISC 360 chapter H3, CSA S16 clause 14.10). Native suffix: Tf.
  • 6 - CombinedForces: The combined-forces interaction equation - axial force with biaxial bending, and with shear and torsion where the code includes them (AISC 360 chapter H, CSA S16 clauses 13.8 / 13.9). Native suffix: FM.

AiscResistanceError.description:
Whether a North American resistance check produced a result, and why not if it did not

Possible values:

  • 0 - None: The check ran and its numbers are a result. Native: ERROR_NONE.
  • 1 - NotDone: The check was not performed, so its action, strength and work ratio are three zeros rather than a utilisation of nil. Native: ERROR_NOT_DONE - and the value every block is initialised to, so it is also what a block the engine never reached reports.
  • 2 - Class: The cross-section could not be classified, so no resistance could be established. The engine returns it from CSectionClassificationAISC::ClassifyCrossSection whenever the class comes out unknown, and from CSectionClassificationS16 for an unknown shape. Native: ERROR_CLASS.
  • 3 - Segments: The member's segmentation between lateral restraints ("troncons") is inconsistent, so the unbraced lengths the flexural checks need could not be established. Native: ERROR_TRONCONS.

AiscResistanceWarning.description:
A note the engine attached to a North American resistance check

Possible values:

  • 0 - None: Nothing to report. Native: WARNING_NONE, and the value every block is initialised to.
  • 1 - SlendernessRatioAbove200: The member's slenderness ratio KL/r exceeds 200. AISC 360 section E2 recommends against it as a user note rather than forbidding it, and CSA S16 clause 10.4.2.1 sets the same limit for compression members, so the resistance below was computed anyway. Native: WARNING_KL_r_200.

AiscSectionPartType.description:
Role a plate of the cross-section plays in its North American classification

Possible values:

  • 0 - Web: A stiffened element - supported along both edges, perpendicular to the bending axis. The web of an I-shape or a channel. Native: WEB.
  • 1 - Flange: An unstiffened element - supported along one edge, parallel to the bending axis. The flange of an I-shape, a channel or an angle leg. Native: FLANGE.
  • 2 - Round: The wall of a round HSS, classified by its diameter-to-thickness ratio rather than by a width-to-thickness one, so it is neither stiffened nor unstiffened. Native: ROUND.

designCode.description:
The steel design code the model is configured with - one of `aisc`,
`aisc_2016`, `can_csa_s16_2009`, `can_csa_s16_2014`,
`can_csa_s16_2019` or `can_csa_s16_2024`. READ ONLY HERE: a value sent in a
`SetModelSettings` request is ignored. It is chosen once, for the session, with
`Environments.DesignCodes.Steel` - which takes five of the six, `can_csa_s16_2024`
being the exception - and comes from the localization when that is left null.



It changes nothing in this object - all six behave identically here - but it is what
tells a caller which edition the model was actually created for.

verification.description: The Verification page. Left untouched when null.

optimization.description: The Optimisation page. Left untouched when null.

profileSorting.description: The Sort profiles page. Left untouched when null.

buckling.description: The Buckling page. Left untouched when null.

angleVerification.description: The Angle verification page. Left untouched when null.

calculationSequence.description: The Calculation sequence page. Left untouched when null.

AiscSteelCalculationSettings.description:
The general settings of the Expert STEEL design calculation of a model designed to a
NORTH-AMERICAN code - the same Calculation Settings dialog of the desktop application, as
that code family sees it.



SIX CODES, ONE SHAPE. AISC 360, AISC 360-16 and the four CAN/CSA S16 editions (2009, 2014,
2019, 2024) share it. That is not a simplification: every place the dialog branches lists
exactly those six together and treats them identically - the same hidden controls on the
Verification page, the same single buckling method, the same six tabs. Read
AD.API.AiscSteelCalculationSettings.DesignCode to know which of the six the model actually carries.



ONE GROUP OF MODEL SETTINGS. This class is the `SteelAiscCalculation` group of
AD.API.ModelSettingsBase: read with
`GetModelSettings(eModelSettingsCategory.SteelAiscCalculation)`, written with
`SetModelSettings`, which takes the group from this object's own type, and put back to
what a new model of this code carries with
`ResetModelSettings(eModelSettingsCategory.SteelAiscCalculation)`.



HOW IT DIFFERS FROM AD.API.Ec3SteelCalculationSettings, tab by tab:



NO Partial safety factors page. `CGrMetalHypothesesCalculSheet` adds it inside a switch
that lists the four Eurocode codes only - a North-American verification works with the
resistance factor phi (LRFD) or the safety factor Omega (ASD) taken from the code itself,
not with a user-editable gamma_M. The gamma fields still exist on the model and are left
untouched by this group.


A Verification page of three properties instead of thirteen - see
AD.API.AiscSteelVerificationSettings.


A Buckling page whose only accepted method is `eMethodBucklingGa_Gb` - see
AD.API.SteelBucklingSettings.Method.


Optimisation, Sort profiles, Angle verification and Calculation sequence are IDENTICAL, and
are literally the same four DTO classes the Eurocode group uses.



NOT HERE: THE Kt / Kz FACTORS. `CGrMetalExpertLTBSettingsPage` holds this family's own
lateral-torsional-buckling inputs (KtOption, KtFactor, KzOption, KzFactor) and the model
stores them, but the page is never added to the Calculation Settings sheet for any steel
code and its own per-code switch is commented out - no user can reach those four values.
Exposing them here would let this API produce a model state the desktop application cannot,
which is the half of the parity rule that is easy to forget. They are round-tripped
untouched. Add the page to the sheet first, then expose them.



DESIGN TEMPLATES ARE A SEPARATE AXIS, and they are NOT covered yet: `som.Role` carries
an `AISCSteelLinearExpertProperties` slot beside the Eurocode one, but
`CreateDesignTemplate` still refuses anything outside the Eurocode family. These
settings apply to the whole model and are read by the design engine whether or not any
element carries a template.



WHEN TO CALL IT. Before `LaunchAnalysis`, for the reason
AD.API.SteelCalculationSettings gives: these values are written to the descriptive
model, and the analysis model copies them while it is built.



All the page sub-objects are optional: a null one leaves that whole page as the model has
it, and inside one a null property leaves that single setting alone.

crossSectionStrength.description: Verify the strength of the cross-sections. On by default.

elementStability.description: Verify the stability of the elements. On by default.

calculationType.description: Which internal forces the verification combines. Oblique bending by default.

AiscSteelVerificationSettings.description:
The Verification page of a model designed to a North-American steel code: which checks the
engine performs, and which internal forces it combines.



THREE PROPERTIES, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE PAGE. The Eurocode version of this page carries
thirteen; `CGrHypothesesMetalVerificationPage::OnInitDialog` hides all the others under
AISC and CAN/CSA, and a hidden control is a setting the desktop application cannot produce:



the fire check and its duration - hidden for the six North-American codes, which have no
fire verification in Advance Design;


the three imperfections, the 2nd order analysis, the columns and beams buckling lengths and
the imperfection generation - hidden for every code outside the Eurocode family, because
they are EN 1993-1-1 5.3 constructs;


the plate (web) buckling method - hidden for every code outside CM66 and the Eurocode
family, because it is EN 1993-1-5. A North-American model therefore keeps
`eMethodWebBucklingUndefined`, which is exactly why that enumeration exposes a
"not decided" member;


the two 2nd-generation Eurocode groups.



The model still STORES all of them, and this API leaves every one of them exactly as it
found it: a read-modify-write of a North-American model touches only the three properties
below, so nothing an older file or a code conversion left behind is disturbed.



Every property is optional, so that a `SetModelSettings` request can change one switch
without restating the rest.

AisiEquation.description:
The AISI S100 equation a cold-formed verification applied

Possible values:

  • 0 - noRef: No equation recorded. Either the check did not run, or its clause offers a single expression and the engine leaves the field alone. Native: noRef, and the value every payload is initialised to.
  • 1 - eqD2_1: Equation (D2-1) - nominal tensile strength, Tn = Ag * Fy. Native: eqD2_1.
  • 2 - eqE2_1: Equation (E2-1) - nominal axial strength for global buckling, Pne. Native: eqE2_1.
  • 3 - eqE3_1_1: Equation (E3.1-1) - nominal axial strength for local buckling, Pnl = Ae * Fn, capped at Pne. Native: eqE3_1_1.
  • 4 - eqE4_1_2: Equation (E4.1-2) - nominal axial strength for distortional buckling, Pnd. Native: eqE4_1_2.
  • 5 - eqF2_1_1: Equation (F2.1-1) - nominal flexural strength for yielding and global buckling, Mne = Sf * Fn, capped at My. Native: eqF2_1_1.
  • 6 - eqF3_1: Equation (F3-1) - nominal flexural strength for local buckling, Mnl = Se * Fn. Native: eqF3_1.
  • 7 - eqF4_1_2: Equation (F4.1-2) - nominal flexural strength for distortional buckling, Mnd. Native: eqF4_1_2.
  • 8 - eqG2_1_1: Equation (G2.1-1) - shear strength governed by yielding, Vn = Vy. Native: eqG2_1_1.
  • 9 - eqG2_1_2: Equation (G2.1-2) - shear strength in the inelastic range, Vn = sqrt(Vcr * Vy). Native: eqG2_1_2.
  • 10 - eqG2_2_1: Equation (G2.2-1) - shear strength of a web with transverse stiffeners, yielding branch, Vn = Vy. Native: eqG2_2_1.
  • 11 - eqG2_2_2: Equation (G2.2-2) - shear strength of a web with transverse stiffeners, inelastic branch. Native: eqG2_2_2.
  • 12 - eqG2_3_1: Equation (G2.3-1) - shear strength governed by elastic buckling, Vn = Vcr. Native: eqG2_3_1.
  • 13 - eqH1_1_1: Equation (H1.1-1) - combined bending and TENSION, the branch that adds the axial term. Native: eqH1_1_1.
  • 14 - eqH1_1_2: Equation (H1.1-2) - combined bending and tension, the branch that subtracts the axial term. Native: eqH1_1_2.
  • 15 - eqH1_2_1: Equation (H1.2-1) - combined bending and COMPRESSION. Native: eqH1_2_1.
  • 16 - eqH2_1: Equation (H2-1) - combined bending and shear, the quadratic interaction. Native: eqH2_1.
  • 17 - eqH2_2: Equation (H2-2) - combined bending and shear, the linear interaction with a limit of 1.3. Native: eqH2_2.
  • 18 - eqH3_1: Equation (H3-1) - combined bending and web crippling, the 0.91 / 1.3 form. Native: eqH3_1.
  • 19 - eqH3_2: Equation (H3-2) - combined bending and web crippling, the 0.88 / 1.46 form. Native: eqH3_2.
  • 20 - eqH3_3: Equation (H3-3) - combined bending and web crippling, the 0.86 / 1.65 form. Native: eqH3_3.
  • 21 - eqH4_1: Equation (H4-1) - combined bending and torsion, the reduction factor form. Native: eqH4_1.
  • 22 - VERIF_NOT_NEEDED: The verification was not necessary - a real value here rather than a count sentinel, exactly as the VERIF_NOT_NECCESSARY of Ec3ColdFormedEquation is. Native: VERIF_NOT_NEEDED.

AisiSupportLocation.description:
Where along the member the load of a web crippling check sits

Possible values:

  • 0 - End: An end reaction or a load within a member depth of the end. Native: SL_END.
  • 1 - Interior: An interior load, far enough from either end for the web to be restrained on both sides. Native: SL_INTERIOR.

AisiVerificationType.description:
Which AISI S100 clause a cold-formed verification result describes

Possible values:

  • 0 - noVerifStrength: No clause recorded. Native: noVerifStrength, and the value the base struct is initialised to.
  • 1 - AxialTension_D2: Chapter D2 - tensile strength on the gross section. Native: AxialTension_D2.
  • 2 - AxialCompression_E2: Chapter E - axial compression, covering global (E2), local (E3) and distortional (E4) buckling. Native: AxialCompression_E2.
  • 3 - BendingMoment_F_XX: Chapter F - flexure about the major axis, covering global (F2), local (F3) and distortional (F4) buckling. Native: BendingMoment_F_XX.
  • 4 - BendingMoment_F_YY: Chapter F - flexure about the minor axis. Native: BendingMoment_F_YY.
  • 5 - Shear_G: Chapter G2 - shear strength of a web. Native: Shear_G.
  • 6 - WebCripgling_G2: Web crippling - the local crushing of a web under a concentrated transverse load. Native: WebCripgling_G2 (the native spelling, kept as is).
  • 7 - CombinedMomentAndAxial_H1: Chapter H1 - combined axial force and bending, in either the tension (H1.1) or the compression (H1.2) form. Native: CombinedMomentAndAxial_H1.
  • 8 - CombinedMomentAndShear_H2: Chapter H2 - combined bending and shear. Native: CombinedMomentAndShear_H2.
  • 9 - CombinedMomentAndWebCrippling_H3: Chapter H3 - combined bending and web crippling. Native: CombinedMomentAndWebCrippling_H3.
  • 10 - CombinedMomentAndTrosion_H4: Chapter H4 - combined bending and torsion. Native: CombinedMomentAndTrosion_H4 (the native spelling, kept as is).

hasAnalysisModel.description:
True when the project holds an analysis model. A model created through this API has none
until `LaunchAnalysis` is called; a project opened from a file has one when it was
ever calculated.



An Advance Design project holds at most ONE analysis model, so this is a plain boolean and
there is nothing to name or select.

Default value: false

meshState.description:
State of the finite element mesh: none, complete, or incomplete. A tri-state and not a
boolean because Advance Design lets a calculation run on an incomplete mesh - see
`eMeshState.mesh_incomplete`.



The values are Advance Design's own (`mesh_no` / `mesh_available` /
`mesh_incomplete`): `eMeshState` shares its definition with the native mesh
enumeration the mesher and the analysis model use, so the two cannot drift.

Default value: eMeshState.mesh_no

femIsCalculated.description:
True when the finite element analysis has been run and produced results - the analysis
model's own `IsAnalysisCalculated` flag, and the precondition
`LaunchDesignCalculation` refuses to run without.

Default value: false

femIsUpToDate.description:
True when the analysis model still matches the finite element results on disk - the
`Updated` property the design engines and the analysis navigator read.



THIS IS NOT A FRESHNESS GUARANTEE IN AN API SESSION, and the reason is worth reading
before it is used as a gate. The flag is set to `true` by a successful solve and set
back to `false` only by the user interface listener that reacts to a model change
(`InvalidateAnalysisModel`, raised by the Advance Design navigator and snap-ins). An
API session installs no such listener, so once `LaunchAnalysis` has succeeded this
stays `true` no matter what is created, updated or deleted afterwards.


`false` is therefore trustworthy - something really did invalidate the model, which
in practice means a project saved stale by the desktop application, or a converted one.
`true` only means "nothing reported an invalidation". If you changed the model
through this API and need results that match it, call `LaunchAnalysis` again; do not
ask this flag.

Default value: false

femCalculatedCasesCount.description:
How many analysis cases - load cases, combinations and envelopes - carry finite element
results. The count of the analyses whose state is "selected, done, OK", which is exactly
the set Advance Design offers in a result table or a report.



0 with AD.API.AnalysisModelStatus.FemIsCalculated true is possible and means the solve succeeded but no
analysis kept its results - read the diagnostics of the last `LaunchAnalysis`.

Default value: 0

design.description:
One entry per material family that has a design engine - always all four of
`DesignCalculationType`, in that order, so a caller can index the list or match on
AD.API.DesignExpertStatus.Family without checking for absent entries. Empty only
when the analysis model could not be read at all.

Default value: four entries, all at their own defaults

hasConstructionStages.description:
True when the model defines construction stages. Read from the analysis model when it is
available, from the descriptive model otherwise - stages are defined on the descriptive
model, so a staged model that was never calculated still reports `true`.

Default value: false

allStagesCalculated.description:
True when every construction stage has been calculated - the condition the design commands
of Advance Design check before they will run on a staged model.


`null` when the question does not apply: when the model defines no stage, or when the
analysis model could not be read. This is not caution - the model itself answers
`true` for a model without stages, because "every stage is calculated" is vacuously
true of no stages, and reporting that `true` would read as "the staged calculation is
done" on a model that has no stages at all.

Default value: null

overallState.description:
The one value most callers need: where the model stands in the work-flow. Derived from the
properties above, which are all on this same object - so nothing is hidden and no second
call is needed to see why.



The rule, first match wins:

1. `NotCreated` - AD.API.AnalysisModelStatus.HasAnalysisModel is false.

2. `OutOfDate` - AD.API.AnalysisModelStatus.FemIsCalculated and not
AD.API.AnalysisModelStatus.FemIsUpToDate.

3. `Calculated` - AD.API.AnalysisModelStatus.FemIsCalculated.

4. `Meshed` - AD.API.AnalysisModelStatus.MeshState is not `mesh_no`.

5. `Created` - otherwise, which also covers an analysis model the session has
not opened and that a status read must not open (a warning in the diagnostics says so).



Note what is NOT in the rule: the design experts. A model can be `Calculated` with
every family uncalculated, and that is the normal state right after `LaunchAnalysis`;
AD.API.AnalysisModelStatus.Design is the answer to that question, and no single summary can carry four
independent booleans.



Note also that an INCOMPLETE mesh does not change the summary: rules 2 to 4 only ask
whether a mesh exists, because Advance Design allows a calculation on an incomplete one.
Read AD.API.AnalysisModelStatus.MeshState when it matters.


`OutOfDate` IS NEVER REPORTED IN A HEADLESS API SESSION. The flag rule 2 tests is
maintained by the desktop application only - see AD.API.AnalysisModelStatus.FemIsUpToDate. It appears
for a project saved stale by Advance Design, or for one converted on open. Do not use the
summary to decide whether YOUR changes have invalidated the results: it cannot know.

Default value: eAnalysisModelState.NotCreated

AnalysisModelStatus.description:
A read-only snapshot of where the current model stands in the mesh -> finite element ->
design chain: whether an analysis model exists, whether it is meshed, whether it was
calculated, which design experts have run, and how construction stages stand.



PURELY A READ. It creates nothing, opens nothing and runs nothing - in particular it does
not open the analysis model when the session has not opened it, and it does not run the model
verification. It is cheap: every value below is a flag or a counter the model already
carries, and no element of the model is visited. Call it as often as you like.



FLAT ON PURPOSE. The mesh, finite element and construction stage values are prefixed
properties rather than sub-objects, so that no caller has to null-check a group before
reading a value that is always there - a generated client cannot express a non-nullable
sub-object. The design families are the one exception: they are a list because there is one
entry per family.



When AD.API.AnalysisModelStatus.HasAnalysisModel is false, nothing below it is meaningful: every value is
at its default. In the one further case where nothing more could be read - an analysis model
the session has not opened, which a status read must not open - the same is true and a
warning in the response diagnostics says so.

CSASteelLinearDesignTemplate.description:
Expert design template for linear STEEL elements verified to CAN/CSA S16 (maps to the AD model
object `som.CSASteelLinearRole`, held by `som.Role` in its
"CSASteelLinearExpertProperties" slot). 


It corresponds to the "Design template description" dialog of Advance Design when the material
is Steel, the element type is Linear and the model's steel design code is a Canadian one. 


The template name is the base-class member AD.API.InformationalElementBase.UserName; it
must be unique among the steel/linear templates of the model and is limited to 50
characters. 


USED BY WHICH DESIGN CODES - this property set is the one Advance Design allocates for
AD.API.SteelDesignCode.can_csa_s16_2009, AD.API.SteelDesignCode.can_csa_s16_2014,
AD.API.SteelDesignCode.can_csa_s16_2019 and
AD.API.SteelDesignCode.can_csa_s16_2024. All four editions share ONE class because they
share one SOM object: `CRoleManager::AddRole` normalizes them to a single "CSA" expert set,
and neither the model nor the property list distinguishes them. Creating this template in a
model configured for any other steel code is refused, because the engine would never allocate
the CAN/CSA property set for it; the response diagnostics then name the active code. 


HOW IT DIFFERS FROM THE AISC LEAF - two things, and only two. The cross-section class keeps the
Eurocode-like Class 1 to Class 4 list, and the imposed effective (Class 4) characteristics below
exist. Everything else is inherited unchanged from
AD.API.NorthAmericanSteelLinearDesignTemplate. Two rows of
AD.API.NorthAmericanSteelLinearDesignTemplate.SteelSpecificProperties are conversely
CAN/CSA-only and are refused on an AD.API.AISCSteelLinearDesignTemplate. 


PROPAGATION - assigning the template to a linear element, or editing the template afterwards,
copies these properties onto the element's own expert properties through the same mechanism the
user interface uses. Editing a template therefore changes every element that references it. 


PARTIAL UPDATE - every group of AD.API.NorthAmericanSteelLinearDesignTemplate is
nullable. On Update, a group left null keeps its stored value. 

Available for the descriptive model only.

designCalculations.description:
The design (Expert) calculations this combination takes part in - the API replacement of the

value listed twice is applied once. 

On Create, null and an empty list both mean "no design calculation at all". 

On Update the two differ: null leaves the selection exactly as it is, so a caller that only
wants to change a load coefficient does not have to restate it, while an empty list is the

whatever was selected before. 

Listing a calculation makes its coefficients mandatory on the AD combination: when the
matching group of AD.API.Combination.ConcreteDesign / AD.API.Combination.SteelDesign /
AD.API.Combination.TimberDesign / AD.API.Combination.CompositeDesign is not supplied and the

updateLoadCaseCodes.description:
Refresh the normative code of every load case from the combination template
before generating (ECG, ECQ, ECN, ...).



Leave it unset - which means `true` - for a model built through the API. The
combination templates match load cases on exactly that code, and a load case
created through the API carries a neutral default one, so a generation with this
turned off returns no combination at all on such a model. Send `false` only
when the codes were already set deliberately and must not be touched, which today
means only a model opened from a project file.



Nullable on purpose, and not a plain `bool` with a default: a generated client
mirrors the property type, not the initializer, so a non-nullable bool would reach
the server as an explicit `false` whenever the caller did not set it - making
the useful default unreachable through the client.

applyDefaultConcomitanceRules.description:
`DetailedMatrix` only: re-apply the default concomitance rules between load
            case families and load cases before generating, which reinitializes the
            concomitance matrix. When `false` - the default - the rules set already stored
            in the model is used as it is, which is what a model opened from a project file
            wants: those rules are what its author set up.

CombinationsGenerationRequest.description:
Input of the automatic combination generation.



Everything the generation needs is read from the model: the per-load-case
coefficients (gamma EQU, gamma STR/GEO, psi0/psi1/psi2, duration, category, ...) live
on the load cases themselves and can be set through
AD.API.LoadCaseCombinationsCoefficients, while the generator options - which
project situations are generated, the per-family coefficient tables, the equation
option - live on the model settings. This request therefore only says WHICH
work-flow to run, not how the standard is parameterized.

createdCombinations.description:
Internal identifiers of the combinations that were created, in generation order.
Read them back with `GetInformationalElementsObject`. Empty when nothing was
generated - the reason is then in the response diagnostics.

firstIdentifier.description:
The user visible number ("No.") of the first generated combination, 0 when

lastIdentifier.description:
The user visible number ("No.") of the last generated combination, 0 when nothing

limitExceeded.description:
True when the generator produced more combinations than the limit configured on
the model (`ModelProperties.MaxNumberMatrixGeneratedCombinations`) and the set
was therefore trimmed to it. AD.API.CombinationsGenerationResult.CreatedCombinations then holds the
combinations that were kept, and the ones beyond the limit do not exist.

CombinationsGenerationResult.description:
Outcome of the automatic combination generation.



Deliberately narrow. The generation either writes combinations or it does not, and
anything else worth knowing about the run - a template that could not be opened, a
model that yields nothing - is reported as a diagnostic in the response details rather
than as a flag here.

The result payload of the operation.
May be `null` or default when AD.API.Srv.Models.ApiResponseDetails.Success is `false`.

details.description: response details for API operations, including the actual result data and structured diagnostics.

Standard envelope returned by every API operation.
Wraps the actual result together with structured diagnostics
(errors, warnings, informational messages) so that callers –

standard.description:
The combination standard the model generates for. READ ONLY HERE - a value sent in a
`SetModelSettings` request is ignored. What decides which settings a request
writes is its `$type`, not this.



It is chosen once, for the session, with `Environments.DesignCodes.Combinations`
on `NewProject` / `OpenProject`, and comes from the localization when that is
left null.

annex.description:
National annex of the Eurocode standard. READ ONLY HERE on the same terms as
AD.API.CombinationsGenerationSettings.Standard - chosen with `Environments.DesignCodes.CombinationsAnnex` -
and null for the standards that have no annex (US, Canada, and the Italian standards,
which differ from Eurocode by standard rather than by annex).



Worth reading before writing live load or snow settings: the annex decides how many
categories exist and what each index means.

CombinationsGenerationSettings.description:
The settings of the automatic ("simplified") combination generation, as they are stored
on the model - the same ones the Combinations options dialog of the desktop application
edits.



These are NOT properties of any combination: they are general options that apply to the
whole model and are read by the generation, so they are set once, before calling
`GenerateCombinations`. What each load case contributes on its own (its gamma, its
psi, its duration) lives on the load case instead, as
`LoadCase.CombinationsCoefficients`.



ONE GROUP OF MODEL SETTINGS. This class is the `CombinationsGeneration` group of
AD.API.ModelSettingsBase - the general settings of the model - so it is read with
`GetModelSettings(eModelSettingsCategory.CombinationsGeneration)`, written with
`SetModelSettings`, which takes the base class and takes the group from this
object's own type, and put back to what the active standard prescribes with
`ResetModelSettings(eModelSettingsCategory.CombinationsGeneration)`.



FIVE SHAPES, FOUR OF THEM REACHABLE. Eurocode, the 2nd generation Eurocode, US, Canada and
EN 13031-1 (greenhouses) share nothing: each has its own set of fields on the model and
its own dialog page. The derived type therefore says which standard the settings belong
to, and AD.API.CombinationsGenerationSettings.Standard says which one the model actually generates for. The 2nd
generation shape is NOT reachable: EN 1990:2023 is not exposed by this API, so
AD.API.eCombinationsStandard has no member for it and a model that carries it is
refused by the read, the write and the reset alike.



HOW THE STANDARD IS CHOSEN. Not here - it is a property of the SESSION, fixed on the
`NewProject` / `OpenProject` call and unchangeable afterwards. By default it is
resolved from the localization passed to `SetEnvironment`: `LOCALIZATION_US` and
`LOCALIZATION_ASIA` give a US standard, `LOCALIZATION_CANADA` a Canadian one,
`LOCALIZATION_ITALIA` gives NTC 2018, and every other localization gives Eurocode
with that country's national annex. WHICH edition of the US and Canadian standards is
the installation's own business - read AD.API.CombinationsGenerationSettings.Standard rather than assuming one.
To choose it instead of inheriting it, set `Environments.DesignCodes.Combinations` on
that same call. EN 13031-1 is reachable only on an installation configured for greenhouses,
whichever way you ask for it: elsewhere its settings can be written and read back, but a
generation will not use them and naming it in `DesignCodes` is refused.



DERIVED COEFFICIENTS. Wherever the standard tabulates a coefficient against a category,
the category decides and the coefficient is read only, exactly as the cell is read only
in the dialog's grid. Sending a value anyway is not an error: it is ignored and reported
as a warning in the response diagnostics. Each category has one "user defined" member
which unlocks its coefficients; that is the only way to impose your own.

CsaCrossSectionClass.description:

Possible values:

  • 0 - Auto: No class determined. Native: CSA_CLASS_AUTO. As with the AISC vocabulary, this is also what a part slot the engine never wrote reads back as, the result struct being zeroed before it is filled.
  • 1 - Class1: Class 1 - plastic. The section can develop its plastic moment with the rotation capacity plastic analysis requires. Native: CSA_CLASS_1.

Material family whose Expert design engine is launched by LaunchDesignCalculation

Possible values:

  • 0 - Concrete: Reinforced concrete design (called "BA" - beton arme - in the AD model): EC2, BAEL, ACI, BS 8110 or STAS, depending on the concrete design code configured on the model.
  • 1 - Steel: Steelwork design: EC3 (1st or 2nd generation), CM66, AISC or CSA, depending on the steel design code configured on the model.
  • 2 - Timber: Timber design: EC5 or the North-American codes (O86 / NDS), depending on the timber design code configured on the model.

combinations.description:
The combination standard - the "Combinations" row (EN 1990 and its relatives).


`Greenhouse_EN13031_1` is accepted only on an installation carrying the greenhouse
licence switch, which is the same condition under which the desktop dialog offers it.



This is the same value `CombinationsGenerationSettings.Standard` reports, and it
decides the shape of that settings group - so set it here, then read the settings back to
see which shape the model has.

combinationsAnnex.description:
National annex of the combination standard. Accepted only with
AD.API.DesignCodes.Combinations = `Eurocode`: `EurocodeItalia` and `NTC2018`
differ from Eurocode by standard rather than by annex, and the US and Canadian standards
have no annex at all.

seismicAnnex.description: National annex of Eurocode 8. Accepted only with AD.API.DesignCodes.Seismic = `en1998_1`.

climatic.description: The snow and wind standard - the "Climatic" row.

climaticAnnex.description:
National annex of Eurocode 1. Accepted with AD.API.DesignCodes.Climatic = `eurocode` (any
value), `pr_en13031_1` (`general` or `france`) and `romania`
(`romania` only - that standard points at the Romanian annex and the snow and wind
accessors read it).

concrete.description: The reinforced concrete standard - the "Reinforced Concrete" row.

concreteAnnex.description:
National annex of Eurocode 2. Accepted with AD.API.DesignCodes.Concrete = `eurocode` (any
value except `italy`) and with `ntc2008` / `ntc2018` (`italy` only,
which those two standards pin anyway).

steel.description:
The steelwork standard - the "Steelwork" row.


`can_csa_s16_2024` is refused: the enumeration is shared with the read-only
`SteelCalculationSettings.DesignCode`, so it lists one value this API will not take
as an input - S16-24 was removed from the desktop dialog and calculates exactly as
`can_csa_s16_2019`. CM66 and the 2nd generation Eurocode are not in the enumeration
at all.



Which steel settings group the model gets follows from this value: the Eurocode family
gives `SteelEc3Calculation`, the North-American one `SteelAiscCalculation`.

steelAnnex.description:
National annex of Eurocode 3. Accepted only with AD.API.DesignCodes.Steel = `eurocode`,
and never with the value `italy` - Italy is a steel standard here, not an annex.

aiscMethod.description:
The AISC 360 design method - ASD (allowable strength) or LRFD (load and resistance
factor) - the "AISC Method" combo of the desktop configuration dialog. Accepted when a
family that reads it is in force: AD.API.DesignCodes.Combinations = `US` or
`US2018` (the dialog shows the combo for those two only, and the US generation
builds ASD or LRFD combinations from it), OR AD.API.DesignCodes.Steel = `aisc` or
`aisc_2016` (what the AISC 360 Experts calculate with). With neither - Eurocode or
Canadian combinations together with a Eurocode or CSA S16 steel standard - nothing reads
it, and it fails the whole call like an annex sent for a standard that has none.
Reported by `GetEnvironment` under exactly the same condition.



Null keeps what the session already holds: `AllowableStrengthDesign` whenever
AD.API.Environments.Localization is sent - a localization resolves it to ASD, as
the desktop dialog does - and otherwise the value this MACHINE is configured with.



WHAT READS IT. The AISC steel and composite design Experts, the NDS timber Expert and
their reports read it from the session. The US combination generation reads the copy the
project carries, and `GenerateCombinations` rewrites that copy with the session's
method first - as the desktop's combination dialog does before every generation - so a
project opened under a different method than it was saved with gets combinations for the
method of the session. This is also the value
`USCombinationsGenerationSettings.AiscDesignMethod` reports, and the only way to
change it.

timberAnnex.description:
National annex of Eurocode 5. Accepted only with AD.API.DesignCodes.Timber = `eurocode`,
and never with the value `italy`.

masonryAnnex.description: National annex of Eurocode 6. Accepted only with AD.API.DesignCodes.Masonry = `eurocode`.

composite.description:
The composite standard - the "Composite" row.



The desktop dialog keeps this row and the steelwork row in step - picking a steel
standard there also picks the composite one. This API writes the two independently, and
reports a WARNING (not an error) when the resulting pair is one the dialog could not have
produced, for instance AD.API.DesignCodes.Steel = `aisc_2016` with
AD.API.DesignCodes.Composite = `eurocode`.

compositeAnnex.description:
National annex of Eurocode 4. Accepted only with AD.API.DesignCodes.Composite =
`eurocode`.

DesignCodes.description:
The design standards and national annexes of the session - the eight rows of the
Localization configuration dialog of the desktop application, one standard each and the
"NAD used for Eurocodes" combo beside it.



EVERY PROPERTY IS NULLABLE, AND NULL IS NOT "UNSET BY MISTAKE" - IT IS THE DEFAULT.
`SetEnvironment` first resolves all eight standards and all eight annexes from
AD.API.Environments.Localization, exactly as the desktop application resolves them
from its installation, and only then overwrites the ones named here. So a null property
leaves that standard at the localization's own default, and an object with every property
null changes nothing at all. There is no "no standard" state to fall into.



WHEN IT IS APPLIED, AND WHEN IT IS NOT. Together with the rest of
AD.API.Environments, on the `NewProject` or `OpenProject` call that OPENS
the session, before the model is created or read. It then lasts exactly as long as that
project: a further `NewProject` or `OpenProject` sent while the project is still
open is REFUSED, because the standards were already read while the open model was built and
will be read again by the combination generation and by the design Experts. Call
`CloseProject` first; the next project takes a new environment. Read back what is in
force with `GetEnvironment`.



AN ANNEX IS NOT ALWAYS APPLICABLE. The desktop dialog hides the annex combo whenever the
standard is not a Eurocode one, and then writes no annex at all. This API refuses an annex
sent for such a standard instead of dropping it, so that a request never half-applies -
sending AD.API.DesignCodes.Concrete = `aci` together with any
AD.API.DesignCodes.ConcreteAnnex fails the whole call and the project is not created. Each
property below says which standards accept it.



THE 2nd GENERATION EUROCODES ARE NOT AVAILABLE THROUGH THIS API, AND ARE NOT VISIBLE IN IT.
They are not released, so no enumeration of this contract carries a member for one - not
the ones written for this class, and not AD.API.SteelDesignCode or
AD.API.eCombinationsStandard, which are shared with the read-only settings. Sending
one is therefore impossible by name and refused by number. A model that already carries one
cannot be described either: `GetEnvironment` reports that one property as null with a
warning naming it, and on any installation that does not have the 2nd generation enabled the
operations that would have to work under it - the combination and steel settings groups,
design templates, `GenerateCombinations`, `LaunchDesignCalculation` and
`GetDesignResults` - refuse the model rather than answer it under the previous
generation of the standard. The same is true of the standards the desktop application no
longer offers - CM66, STAS 10107, BS 8110, CSA O86-24, CSA S16-19 composite.



SEND ENUMERATORS BY NAME, NEVER BY NUMBER. The numbers in the generated "Possible values"
documentation are Advance Design's own storage values, and three of these enumerations are
deliberately not contiguous because the unavailable standards were left out of them. The
generated clients renumber their copy from 0, so a number copied out of the documentation
and cast into a client enumeration lands on a DIFFERENT standard. A number that is not a
member at all is refused with an error rather than accepted.



TWO THINGS ARE ONLY EVER SAID AS WARNINGS: a property reported as null because the session
carries a standard this API cannot name, and a steelwork / composite pair the desktop
application could not have produced. Both are dropped from the response at
`LogVerbosity` = `Errors`, which is what makes them look like they never happened.
Use `ErrorsAndWarnings` if either matters.

family.description:
Which material family this entry describes.

Default value: DesignCalculationType.Concrete

isCalculated.description:
True when the design engine of this family has produced design results on the model.



This is the engine's OWN flag on `som.ModelProperties` - the same one
`LaunchDesignCalculation` returns as its verdict and the same one the Advance Design
user interface reads to decide whether design results exist:
`CalculationReinforcementDone`, `CalculationSteelDone`,
`CalculationTimberDone`, `CalculationCompositeDone`. The API and the application
therefore agree on what "calculated" means.



IT IS NOT A PROOF THAT DESIGN RESULTS ARE ON DISK. The flag is a boolean the model stores,
and the desktop application writes it on one path that never calculated anything: closing
the Advanced stability dialog of a linear element re-writes `CalculationSteelDone` as
"nothing relevant changed", so a project saved from the user interface can report the
steel family calculated without a single steel result. That path does not exist in an API
session, so a model calculated entirely through this API is not affected - but a model
opened from a project file may be. When it has to be certain, read the results
(`GetDesignResults`) rather than this flag.



Default value: false

settingsChangedSinceCalculation.description:
True when the CALCULATION SETTINGS of this family were changed after the design was last
calculated, so the results no longer match the settings that would be used now. The model
flags `IsHypothesesDeCalculMetalModified`, `IsHypothesesDeCalculTimberModified`
and `IsHypothesesDeCalculCompositeModified`.


`null` means the model does not track this for the family: it is ALWAYS null for
`DesignCalculationType.Concrete`, which has no such flag in the model schema (concrete
has `VerificationModelBA` and `ErrorsOnCalculBA` instead, and neither means "the
settings changed since the calculation"). Nothing is missing from this API - the
information does not exist.



ONLY THE DESKTOP APPLICATION MAINTAINS THESE FLAGS. They are raised by the Calculation
Settings dialog when it detects a changed control, and cleared by the design engines.
`SetModelSettings` does NOT raise them, so in an API-only session this stays
`false` even right after the steel calculation settings were rewritten. Treat
`true` as reliable and `false` as "nothing was reported", not as "nothing
changed".



Default value: null

DesignExpertStatus.description:
State of the Expert design calculation of ONE material family, as part of
AD.API.AnalysisModelStatus. One entry per `DesignCalculationType` is always
returned, including for families the model contains no element of - a family with nothing to
calculate simply reports `IsCalculated = false`.



The family is named by the SAME enumeration `LaunchDesignCalculation` takes, so reading a
state and launching a calculation use one vocabulary: whatever appears here can be launched,
and whatever can be launched appears here.

DesignParameterUnitType.description:
What kind of quantity a reported value is, and therefore its base SI unit

Possible values:

  • 0 - InequalitySign: The value is the sign of an inequality (<, =, >) rather than a physical quantity. Native: eInequalitySign.
  • 1 - Force: Force, in N. Native: eForce.
  • 2 - Moment: Bending moment, in N*m. Native: eMoment.
  • 3 - BiMoment: Bi-moment (warping moment), in N*m^2. Native: eBiMoment.
  • 4 - Pressure: Stress or pressure, in N/m^2. Native: ePressure.
  • 5 - Adimensional: Dimensionless. Work ratios are reported dimensionless in the range 0..1 - they are NOT multiplied by 100. Native: eAdimensional.
  • 6 - LengthFeature: Length of a cross-section feature (fillet radius, flange outstand), in m. Native: eLengthFeatures.
  • 7 - LengthDimension: Overall cross-section dimension (height, width, thickness), in m. Native: eLengthDimension.
  • 8 - LengthElement: Length measured along the member (member length, buckling length), in m. Native: eLengthElement.
  • 9 - Area: Area, in m^2. Native: eArea.
  • 10 - SectionModulus: Section modulus, in m^3. Native: eResistanceModule.
  • 11 - Inertia: Second moment of area, in m^4. Native: eInertia.
  • 12 - WarpingConstant: Warping constant, in m^6. Native: eWarpingConstant.
  • 13 - Text: The symbol is enumerated text rather than a number (a cross-section class, a buckling curve, an LTB method). The numeric value is the corresponding Ec3G2Symbol member. Native: eString.
  • 14 - None: No unit assigned. Native: eNone.

assignmentNumber.description:

"AssignmentNumber"). 

Output only: the engine maintains this counter when a template is assigned to or removed from
an element. A value sent on Create or Update is ignored. A template whose assignment number is
greater than zero can still be deleted; the elements that used it silently fall back to the
built-in default template and keep their current design properties. 

Default value : 0

DesignTemplate.description:
Base class of every Expert design template (maps to the AD model object `som.Role`, called a
"Role" in the code and a "Design template" in the user interface). 


A design template is a named set of design (Expert) properties that lives in a single
model-level pool and is then referenced by any number of structural elements - editing a
template therefore changes every element that uses it. The properties themselves are NOT on this
class: they live on the leaf class of the hierarchy, because they depend both on the material
family and on the design code configured on the model. The hierarchy is 
`DesignTemplate` -> per element type -> per material family -> per design code, e.g.
AD.API.EC3SteelLinearDesignTemplate. 


The template name is the base-class member AD.API.InformationalElementBase.UserName, which
for this entity maps to the "Name" field of the role object (NOT to "FullName" as it does for the
other informational elements). It must be unique for a given (material family, element type) pair
and is limited to 50 characters. 


Every model always contains one built-in default template (displayed as "None"). It belongs to no
material family nor element type - both AD.API.DesignTemplate.MaterialType and AD.API.DesignTemplate.ElementType
read back as the "undefined" value - and it can neither be modified nor deleted through the API.
Assigning it to an element detaches the element from any real template, and deliberately leaves
the element's own design properties untouched. 


List the templates of a model by querying
`InformationalElementTypeEnum.DesignTemplate`. 

Available for the descriptive model only.

DesignTemplateElementType.description:
Kind of structural element a design template applies to

Possible values:

  • 0 - linear: Template applicable to linear elements (beams, columns, bars). Called "eRoleBeam" in the model. This is the only element type currently writable through the API.
  • 1 - planar: Template applicable to planar elements (walls, slabs). Called "eRoleWall" in the model.
  • -1 - undefined_element: Not a real element type: the sentinel carried by the built-in default template ("None").

DesignTemplateMaterialType.description:
Material family a design template applies to

Possible values:

  • 0 - concrete: Reinforced concrete design template (called "BA" - beton arme - in the AD model).
  • 1 - steel: Steel design template. This is the only material family currently writable through the API.
  • 2 - timber: Timber design template.
  • 3 - composite: Composite beam (steel + concrete slab) design template.
  • 4 - rigid: Rigid element design template.
  • -1 - undefined_material: Not a real material family: the sentinel carried by the built-in default template ("None"), which belongs to no family and cannot be modified through the API.

designInMainAxesUuVv.description:
Whether the design is carried out in the principal u-v axes (maps to
"DesignInMainAxesuuvv"). 

READ-ONLY IN PRACTICE - true is REFUSED. Advance Design withdrew this row from the design
template and from the linear element alike (it is hidden unconditionally in both property
lists), so a template can only ever hold false, which is what the engine stamps when it creates
one. It is exposed here so that a GET reports the stored value and a GET-then-PUT round trip
keeps working, not so that it can be changed. 

The reason a non-default value is refused rather than accepted: the option survives as the
slave of the linear element's own "Product of inertia Iyz = 0" row, and assigning a template
copies it onto the element AND overwrites that row with its inverse. Writing true here would
therefore silently clear "Product of inertia Iyz = 0" on every element using the template - a
state no dialog can display or undo. Set the element property instead - it is the same option
inverted, exposed as `LinearElementInnertia.ProductOfInertiaIyz0` on the linear
element. 

Default value : false

(it writes "BucklingChecking" = true on the element's buckling group). Setting it therefore has
an effect, but an indirect one - prefer
AD.API.SteelLinearBuckling.ElementVerification to turn the buckling check on. 

Default value : false

Lateral-torsional buckling length of the UPPER flange (maps to "Lds", from the French
"longueur de deversement superieure").

of AD.API.EC3SteelLateralTorsionalBucklingLength.UpperFlangeParameters - Advance Design stores it twice, and its dialog derives
this one from the other when it closes. There are therefore two ways to set it, and both work: 
send this length ALONE and the flange's mode switches to "imposed" with it, exactly as typing it
in the property list does; or send the flange's own mode and value and leave this at 0, and it
is derived - under the Eurocode as the flange's length when the mode is imposed, and as 0
otherwise. 

Either way the 0 default is never taken literally, so an update that sends this group without
AD.API.EC3SteelLateralTorsionalBucklingLength.UpperFlangeParameters keeps the stored length. Note that SENDING that flange
group does reset the properties of the flange you leave unset, as every group does.
