under the 2nd generation Eurocode 3 - which this API does not expose - the very same stored integer is
interpreted against a DIFFERENT and longer list, which agrees with the 1st-generation one only
on AD.API.SteelLtbCurveMethod.general_case. On a 2nd-generation model
AD.API.SteelLtbCurveMethod.least_favorable therefore selects the buckling of the
compression flange, and AD.API.SteelLtbCurveMethod.most_favorable selects the least
favourable method; the 2nd generation's own "most favourable" is
AD.API.SteelLtbCurveMethod.second_generation_most_favorable, which does not exist under
the 1st generation. Read the full ordinal-by-ordinal table on
AD.API.SteelLtbCurveMethod before setting this on a 2nd-generation model. 

Note also that Advance Design stores AD.API.SteelLtbCurveMethod.least_favorable in every
newly created template whatever the generation, and never converts a template's value when the
model switches generation, so a 2nd-generation template starts out on the buckling of the
compression flange rather than on the 2nd generation's default.

EC3SteelLinearDesignTemplate.description:
Expert design template for linear STEEL elements verified to the EUROCODE (maps to the AD model
object `som.EC3SteelLinearRole`, held by `som.Role` in its
"EC3SteelLinearExpertProperties" slot). 


This is the leaf of the design-template hierarchy and the class that actually carries the design
properties. It corresponds to the "Design template description" dialog of Advance Design when the
material is Steel, the element type is Linear and the model's steel design code is a Eurocode
one. 


The template name is the base-class member AD.API.InformationalElementBase.UserName; it
must be unique among the steel/linear templates of the model and is limited to 50
characters. 


USED BY WHICH DESIGN CODES - this property set is the one Advance Design allocates for
AD.API.SteelDesignCode.eurocode,
AD.API.SteelDesignCode.ntc2008 and AD.API.SteelDesignCode.ntc2018. Creating this
template in a model configured for any other steel code is refused, because the engine would
never allocate the Eurocode property set for it; the response diagnostics then name the active
code. A few properties are further restricted to the 2nd-generation Eurocode and are documented
as such. 


PROPAGATION - assigning the template to a linear element, or editing the template afterwards,
copies these properties onto the element's own expert properties through the same mechanism the
user interface uses. Editing a template therefore changes every element that references it. 


PARTIAL UPDATE - every group below is nullable. On Update, a group left null keeps its stored
value, so a caller can patch one group without restating the rest. Lists inside a group are the
exception: when a list is sent it replaces the stored one in full. 

Available for the descriptive model only.

Ec3G2Message.description:
Status note or warning attached to one equation of a verification

Possible values:

  • 0 - None: No message. Native: NO_MESSAGE.
  • 1 - Class4Tube: Class 4 tubular section. Native: CLASS_4_TUBE.
  • 2 - Class4Rectangular: Class 4 rectangular section. Native: CLASS_4_RECT.
  • 3 - Class4Circular: Class 4 circular section. Native: CLASS_4_CIRC.
  • 4 - Class4Other: Class 4 section of another shape. Native: CLASS_4_OTHER.
  • 5 - Class4TubeCompressionOnly: Class 4 tubular sections are only verified in pure compression. Native: IS_WARNING_CLASS_4_TUBE.
  • 6 - OvalCompressionLimitExceeded: The CTICM condition on the axial force of an oval section is not met (0 <= NEd / Npl <= 0.3). Native: OVAL_COMPRESSION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
  • 7 - OvalBendingLimitExceeded: The CTICM condition on the weak-axis bending moment of an oval section is not met. Native: OVAL_BENDING_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
  • 8 - OvalReducedSlendernessLimitExceeded: The reduced slenderness of an oval section exceeds the limit. Native: OVAL_REDUCED_SLENDERNESS_LIMIT.
  • 9 - ShearBucklingRequired: The shear buckling slenderness screen of EN 1993-1-1 equation 8.27 requires a shear buckling check. Native: SHEAR_BUCKLING_REQUIRED.
  • 10 - ShearBucklingNotRequired: The shear buckling slenderness screen of EN 1993-1-1 equation 8.27 does not require a shear buckling check. Native: SHEAR_BUCKLING_NOT_REQUIRED.
  • 11 - OvalBendingAxialCheckNotPerformed: The bending and axial check was not performed because the oval interaction ratio n,Ov is below 1. Native: OVAL_BENDING_AXAL_NOV_CHECK_NOT_DONE.
  • 12 - ShearAndBendingRequired: Clause 8.2.8(3): the shear force must be accounted for in the design moment resistance (equation 8.35). Native: SHEAR_AND_BENDING_IS_REQUIRED_eq8_35.
  • 13 - ShearAndBendingNotRequired: Clause 8.2.8(3): the effect of the shear force on the design moment resistance may be neglected (equation 8.35). Native: SHEAR_AND_BENDING_IS_NOT_REQUIRED_eq8_35.
  • 14 - ShearReductionFactorOutOfRange: Clause 8.2.8(4), equation 8.37: rho > 1.0, the check cannot be performed. Native: WARNING_8_2_8_4.
  • 15 - TorsionNotVerifiedForSection: Torsion is not verified for this type of cross-section. Native: NO_TORSION_FOR_THIS_SECTION.
  • 16 - TorsionModulusNotDefined: The torsion modulus wt is not defined for this cross-section. Native: WT_NOT_DEFINED.
  • 17 - TorsionShearReductionRequired: Clause 8.2.8: the moment resistance must be reduced for the shear force (VEd > etaV * Vpl,T,Rd). Native: TORSION_SHEAR_REDUCTION_REQUIRED.
  • 18 - TorsionShearReductionNotRequired: Clause 8.2.8: no reduction of the moment resistance for the shear force is required. Native: TORSION_SHEAR_REDUCTION_NOT_REQUIRED.
  • 19 - BucklingSlendernessBelowLimit: The slenderness is below the limit, so the buckling check is not necessary. Native: FLEXURAL_BUCKLING_SLENDERNESS_OK.
  • 20 - OutOfScope: The configuration is outside the scope of the design code. Native: OUT_OF_SCOPE.
  • 21 - ConditionsFulfilled: The conditions of the clause are fulfilled. Native: CONDITIONS_FULLFILLED (native spelling).
  • 22 - AxialReductionRequired: Equations 8.45, 8.46 and 8.47: the moment resistance must be reduced for the axial force. Native: REDUCTION_FROM_AXIAL_REQUIRED.
  • 23 - AxialReductionNotRequired: Equations 8.45, 8.46 and 8.47: no reduction of the moment resistance for the axial force is required. Native: REDUCTION_FROM_AXIAL_NOT_REQUIRED.
  • 24 - AxialForceExceedsPlasticResistance: Clause 8.2.9.1(5): NEd is greater than Npl,Rd, the check cannot be performed. Native: NED_GREATER_THAN_NPLRD.
  • 25 - CheckNotRequired: The check is not required. Native: CHECK_NOT_REQUIRED.
  • 26 - WebShearBucklingCheckRequired: EN 1993-1-5:2024 section 7.1(2): the web shear buckling check is required. Distinct from
  • 27 - WebShearBucklingCheckNotRequired: EN 1993-1-5:2024 section 7.1(2): the web shear buckling check is not required. Native: SB_WEB_CHECK_NOT_REQUIRED.
  • 28 - WebShearBucklingFlangesContribute: The flanges can contribute to the shear buckling resistance (MEd <= Mf,Rd). Native: SB_FLANGES_CAN_CONTRIBUTE.
  • 29 - WebShearBucklingFlangesDoNotContribute: The flanges cannot contribute to the shear buckling resistance (MEd > Mf,Rd). Native: SB_FLANGES_CANNOT_CONTRIBUTE.
  • 30 - WebShearBucklingInteractionNotRequired: EN 1993-1-5:2024 section 9.1: the interaction check is not required (eta3 <= 0.5). Native: SB_INTERACTION_NOT_REQUIRED.
  • 31 - WebShearBucklingEta1LowerBounded: eta1 was below Mf,Rd / Meff,Rd and has been lower-bounded to that ratio. Native: SB_ETA1_LOWER_BOUNDED.

and 1; 0.5 by default.

Ec3G2VerificationId.description:
Which design check an EN 1993 2nd generation verification result describes

Possible values:

  • 0 - None: No verification. Native: noVerifID.
  • 1 - AxialTension: Axial tension resistance, clause 8.2.3. Native: REZ_Tension.
  • 2 - AxialCompression: Axial compression resistance, clause 8.2.4. Native: REZ_Compression.
  • 3 - ShearY: Shear resistance along the y-y axis, clause 8.2.6. Native: REZ_ShearForce_Y.
  • 4 - ShearZ: Shear resistance along the z-z axis, clause 8.2.6. Native: REZ_ShearForce_Z.
  • 5 - BendingYY: Bending resistance about the y-y axis, clause 8.2.5. Native: REZ_BendingMoment_YY.
  • 6 - BendingZZ: Bending resistance about the z-z axis, clause 8.2.5. Native: REZ_BendingMoment_ZZ.
  • 7 - BendingYYAndAxial: Bending about y-y combined with axial force, clause 8.2.9. Native: REZ_Bending_YY_Axial.
  • 8 - BendingZZAndAxial: Bending about z-z combined with axial force, clause 8.2.9. Native: REZ_Bending_ZZ_Axial.
  • 9 - BiaxialBending: Biaxial bending, clause 8.2.9. Native: REZ_Bending_Biaxial.
  • 10 - BendingYYAndShearZ: Bending about y-y combined with shear along z, clause 8.2.8. Native: REZ_Bending_YY_Shear_Z.
  • 11 - BendingZZAndShearY: Bending about z-z combined with shear along y, clause 8.2.8. Native: REZ_Bending_ZZ_Shear_Y.
  • 12 - BendingYYShearZAndAxial: Bending about y-y combined with shear along z and axial force. Native: REZ_Bending_YY_Shear_Z_Axial.
  • 13 - BendingZZShearYAndAxial: Bending about z-z combined with shear along y and axial force. Native: REZ_Bending_ZZ_Shear_Y_Axial.
  • 14 - BiaxialBendingShearAndAxial: Biaxial bending combined with shear and axial force. Native: REZ_Bending_Biaxial_Shear_Axial.
  • 15 - Torsion: Torsion resistance, clause 8.2.7. Native: REZ_Torsion.
  • 16 - TorsionAndBendingYY: Torsion combined with bending about y-y, clause 8.2.7. Native: REZ_Torsion_Bending_YY.
  • 17 - TorsionAndShearZ: Torsion combined with shear along z, clause 8.2.7. Native: REZ_Torsion_Shear_Z.

Ec3SteelCalculationSettings.description:
The steel calculation settings of a model designed to Eurocode 3 - either generation, and
including the Italian NTC standards, which are national applications of it.



One sub-object per page of the Calculation Settings dialog. All of them are optional: a
null sub-object leaves that whole page as the model has it, and inside a sub-object a null
property leaves that one setting alone. So changing a single switch is a request carrying
one sub-object with one property in it.



PREFER A PARTIAL REQUEST TO A WHOLE-OBJECT ECHO. Posting back everything a
`GetModelSettings` returned works and changes nothing, but it will report a handful of
advisory warnings: several properties are only read while another switch is on - the fire
time, the optimisation thresholds, the iteration ceiling, the profile limits, the
complete-calculation count - and the 2nd-generation sub-objects are not read at all on a
1st-generation model. Sending only what you mean to change keeps the diagnostics meaningful.

option.description: Whether the factors come from the code or from this request. `eSafetyFactorsAuto` by default.

gammaM0.description:
gamma_M0 - resistance of cross-sections. Writable only when AD.API.Ec3SteelSafetyFactorSettings.Option is
`eSafetyFactorsImposed`.

gammaM1.description:
gamma_M1 - resistance to instability. Writable only when AD.API.Ec3SteelSafetyFactorSettings.Option is
`eSafetyFactorsImposed`.

gammaM2.description:
gamma_M2 - resistance of the net section at bolt holes, used by the angle
verification. Writable only when AD.API.Ec3SteelSafetyFactorSettings.Option is `eSafetyFactorsImposed`.

gammaMfi.description:
gamma_M,fi - the accidental fire situation. Writable only when AD.API.Ec3SteelSafetyFactorSettings.Option is
`eSafetyFactorsImposed`.

secondGeneration.description:
The 2nd generation addition to this page. Left untouched when null, and ignored with a
warning when the model is not a 2nd generation one.

Ec3SteelSafetyFactorSettings.description:
The Safety factors page: the partial safety factors of EN 1993-1-1.



DERIVED UNLESS IMPOSED. While AD.API.Ec3SteelSafetyFactorSettings.Option is `eSafetyFactorsAuto` the four gamma values are
what the steel code and its national annex dictate, and they are READ ONLY - exactly as the
dialog greys the fields out. Sending one anyway is not an error: it is dropped and reported
as a warning in the response diagnostics. Set AD.API.Ec3SteelSafetyFactorSettings.Option to `eSafetyFactorsImposed` to
write your own; that can be done in the same request.



The defaults are 1.00 for all of them except gamma_M2, which is 1.25, with two national
exceptions the engine applies on its own: the German annex raises gamma_M1 to 1.10 and
gamma_Mfi to 1.15, and the Italian annex and the NTC standards raise gamma_M0 and gamma_M1
to 1.05.

fireResistanceTime.description:
Fire resistance duration, IN SECONDS. The desktop dialog shows it in minutes; this is
the stored SI value, so 30 minutes is 1800. 0 by default.



Read only while AD.API.Ec3SteelVerificationSettings.FireVerification is on - the dialog greys the field out
otherwise - so a duration sent with the check off is stored and reported as a warning.

globalSwayImperfections.description: Account for global sway imperfections. Off by default.

localBowImperfections.description: Account for local bow imperfections. Off by default.

crownImperfections.description:
Account for the crown imperfection of EN 13031-1. Offered only by installations
configured for greenhouses; stored otherwise, but nothing reads it.

secondOrderAnalysis.description:
Run a 2nd order analysis for the static combinations.



FORCED OFF when no imperfection is enabled. The dialog does not merely disable this box
in that state, it clears it - so a model carrying a 2nd order analysis with no
imperfection is one the desktop application cannot hold, and a request that would
produce it has the flag turned off and reported as a warning.

columnsBucklingLength.description:
Where the buckling length of the columns comes from. `imposed` ("buckling length = element properties") by default.



Read only while ANY of the three imperfections is enabled -
AD.API.Ec3SteelVerificationSettings.GlobalSwayImperfections, AD.API.Ec3SteelVerificationSettings.LocalBowImperfections or
AD.API.Ec3SteelVerificationSettings.CrownImperfections. Sent with all three off, it is stored and reported.

beamsBucklingLength.description:
Where the buckling length of the beams comes from. `imposed` ("buckling length = element properties") by default.



A NARROWER CONDITION than the columns one: the dialog enables the beams group on
AD.API.Ec3SteelVerificationSettings.LocalBowImperfections alone, so the global sway and crown imperfections do
not unlock it. Sent with the local bow off, it is stored and reported.

imperfectionGeneration.description:
Which combinations the imperfections are generated for.
`eImperfectionGenerationForGoverningComb` by default on a Eurocode model.



Read only while any of the three imperfections is enabled, like
AD.API.Ec3SteelVerificationSettings.ColumnsBucklingLength. `eImperfectionGenerationUndefined` cannot be chosen: it means "no
option selected", which only a model created under a steel code that has no
imperfection generation carries.

plateBucklingMethod.description:
How a slender web is verified. `eMethodWebBucklingEffectiveCrossSections` by default on a Eurocode model.


`eMethodWebBucklingReducedStresses` is accepted everywhere but reported as a warning under the Czech
and Slovak national annexes, whose EN 1993-1-5 recommendations restrict it - the same
message the dialog shows. `eMethodWebBucklingUndefined` cannot be chosen, for the reason
AD.API.Ec3SteelVerificationSettings.ImperfectionGeneration gives.

systemIDs.description:
Internal ids (AD.API.EID) of the systems (`som.System`) this element belongs to.
An element can belong to several systems. 

- On Get: populated with the element's current systems. 

- On Create: the element is created in the first listed system and added to the rest; when
  empty, it is placed in the model's default root system ("Structure 0"); a listed id that is not an existing system makes the creation fail. 

- On Update: when non-empty, the element's membership is set to exactly these systems (added
  to the new ones, removed from the others); when empty, the membership is left unchanged.
  Invalid system ids are rejected (the update fails without changing any membership). 

- The element always belongs to at least one system: it can never be left with none. If it
  would be (its systems were deleted, or the requested membership could not be applied), it is
  put back in the root system "Structure 0" and a warning is logged.

section.description:
EID of the section already created (required).

When the linear element is a variable beam (GeneralBeamType is variablebeam / poutre_inertie_variable
or CompositeBeamVariable) this represents the cross-section at the Start extremity of the element.
For any other beam type it represents the cross-section applied over the whole length of the element.

sectionEnd.description:
EID of the section at the End extremity of the element.

Only taken into account when the element is a variable beam (GeneralBeamType is variablebeam /
poutre_inertie_variable or CompositeBeamVariable); in that case it defines the cross-section at the
End extremity while 'section' defines the Start extremity. The Start and End sections of a variable
beam must be of the same section type (family) — if they differ an error is raised and the request is
rejected: on creation no element is created, and on update the End section is left unchanged. For any
other beam type it must be identical to 'section' — if a different (non-zero) value is supplied it is
ignored, a warning is raised, and the Start section is used for both extremities.

designTemplateId.description:
Internal id (AD.API.EID) of the Expert design template assigned to this element, i.e. of
the AD.API.LinearDesignTemplate whose design properties are applied to it. 


The element holds a REFERENCE, not a copy: assigning a template, or editing the template
afterwards, copies the template's design properties onto the element's own expert properties. 


The template must match the element, on all three of the following conditions, otherwise the
assignment is refused with an error in the response diagnostics and nothing is changed: 

- it is a template of LINEAR elements; 

- it is of the SAME MATERIAL FAMILY as the element. Note that a steel element modelled as a
  composite beam (LinearElementType = eLinearElementFEMTypeCompositeBeam) belongs to the composite
  family, so a steel template cannot be assigned to it; 

- it carries the property set of the DESIGN CODE the model is configured with at the moment of the
  assignment. A template only ever holds the properties of the code that was active when it was
  created, so one created under another code cannot be applied until it is converted. 


- On Get: the id of the currently assigned template, or 0 when the element is on the built-in
  default template ("None"). 

- On Create / Update: null leaves the assignment untouched; a valid id assigns that template;
  0 detaches the element back to the default template. 


Note that detaching is deliberately NOT a reset: Advance Design keeps the element's current
expert property values when the default template is assigned, so that hand-made changes survive.


CHANGING THE MATERIAL of the element DROPS its design template: Advance Design recreates the
expert object of the new material, so the assignment is lost and is not restored by switching the
material back. Re-assign the template after a material change. 


Default value: null (assignment left unchanged)

systemIDs.description:
Internal ids (AD.API.EID) of the systems (`som.System`) this element belongs to.
An element can belong to several systems. 

- On Get: populated with the element's current systems. 

- On Create: the element is created in the first listed system and added to the rest; when
  empty, it is placed in the model's default root system ("Structure 0"); a listed id that is not an existing system makes the creation fail. 

- On Update: when non-empty, the element's membership is set to exactly these systems (added
  to the new ones, removed from the others); when empty, the membership is left unchanged.
  Invalid system ids are rejected (the update fails without changing any membership). 

- The load area always belongs to at least one system: it can never be left with none. If it
  would be (its systems were deleted, or the requested membership could not be applied), it is
  put back in the root system "Structure 0" and a warning is logged.

selectedReleaseName.description:
Name of the AD.API.LinearReleaseTemplate applied to every edge of the element.

This is the "Releases / Side" property of the AD user interface.

- On Get: the value stored on the element - the name of a template when all the edges share
  the same one, a localized "Other" when they differ, and empty for an element whose releases
  were never initialized. AD.API.ElementPlanar.LinearReleases always holds the authoritative per-edge state.

- On Create: when omitted, the built-in "Fixed" template is applied to every edge, exactly like
  for an element created in AD. A value that names no existing template falls back to "Fixed"
  and a warning is logged - the element is still created.

- On Update: null or an empty string leaves the current assignment unchanged; a non-empty value
  must name a template that exists in the model, otherwise it is ignored and a warning is logged.

- Setting it applies that template to ALL the edges and therefore takes precedence over
  AD.API.ElementPlanar.LinearReleases when both are provided, on Create as well as on Update; sending
  both logs a warning. Send AD.API.ElementPlanar.LinearReleases alone to define a per-edge assignment.

Because the names of the three built-in templates are localized, the invariant keywords "free",
"pinned" and "fixed" are also accepted (case-insensitive) and resolved to the corresponding
built-in template.

Default value: null

linearReleases.description:
Internal ids (AD.API.EID) of the AD.API.LinearReleaseTemplate applied to each edge
of the element, one entry per edge, in edge order: `LinearReleases[i]` is the edge going from
`GeomPtsList[i]` to `GeomPtsList[i+1]`, the last one closing back on `GeomPtsList[0]`.

This is the per-side definition of the AD "Releases / Definition" dialog.

- On Get: the complete edge list of the element (null only when the element has no releases at all).

- On Create / Update: optional. When supplied, the number of entries must equal the number of
  edges of the element and every id must be an existing template, otherwise the whole list is
  rejected, an error is logged and no edge is changed - never a partial assignment.

- Ignored when AD.API.ElementPlanar.SelectedReleaseName is also set.

- On Update, an element whose releases were never initialized (created by an API build older than
  this feature) is initialized with the default template first, so the per-edge assignment applies.

- When an Update changes AD.API.ElementPlanar.GeomPtsList in a way that changes the NUMBER of edges, the
  indices no longer designate the same physical sides, so every edge is RESET to the built-in "Fixed"
  template and a warning is logged. A contour change that keeps the same number of edges leaves the
  releases in place (they stay attached to the same edge index), like the interactive model does.
  To keep or apply a specific assignment across an edge-count change, send it - this property or
  AD.API.ElementPlanar.SelectedReleaseName - in the SAME update; an explicit request always wins over the reset.

Use the templates already defined in the model: list them with a query on
`InformationalElementTypeEnum.LinearReleaseTemplate`, or create your own with
`CreateInformationalElement`.

Default value: null

geomPtsList.description: Geometry defined by a 3D point list in the global axis system, in drawing order: the poly line is the chain of straight segments `GeomPtsList[0] -> GeomPtsList[1] -> ... `, so N points give N-1 segments. The rules are exactly the ones of the interactive Polyline command, and nothing more: - At least 2 points. A shorter list is refused: the element is not created, and on Update nothing at all is modified (the element keeps its previous geometry). - A point coincident with the one before it is DROPPED, not refused - Advance Design skips the zero-length segment the same way. The dropped points are reported as a warning, and both the read-back geometry and AD.API.PolyLineMeshProperties.DetailedMeshStylePerEdge are indexed on the segments that remain. A list where nothing survives (every point coincident with the previous one, so no segment at all) is refused. Everything else is accepted, exactly like in Advance Design: - Aligned points are fine - any number of them. They simply make collinear segments; alignment is only used internally to pick a non-degenerate local frame. - The poly line is not required to be planar and may cross itself. - There is no maximum number of points. Unlike the contour of a planar element, a poly line is NOT implicitly closed. To close it, repeat the first point as the last one; a closed poly line reads back the same way, with the closing point repeated, so `GeomPtsList.Count - 1` is always the number of segments. Unit: m

ElementPolyLine.description:
Geometric poly line element - the "Polyline" object of Advance Design (`som.EFFacadeCurve`),
listed as "Line" in the model tree.


A poly line has no stiffness, no material, no section and carries no load: it is a chain of
straight segments used as reference geometry - to drive the mesh (it forces FE nodes along its
segments when AD.API.PolyLineMeshProperties.MeshActive is set) and to snap or construct
other elements onto it.

Its geometry is given as a point list exactly like AD.API.ElementPlanar, but it is only
the outline: it is NOT closed, NOT required to be planar, and may intersect itself. See
AD.API.ElementPolyLine.GeomPtsList.

Poly lines are created, read, updated, queried and deleted through the same generic element
endpoints as every other element; query them with
`ElementTypeEnum.ElementPolyLine`.

language.description:
Language used in environment.



FIXED FOR THE LIFE OF THE SERVER PROCESS, not of the session: the first environment
settles it and a later one naming a different language is refused. Null means "whatever
the server is already running in", which is always accepted. See the remarks on
AD.API.Environments.

localization.description:
Localization setting for norms and regulations. It resolves all eight design standards and
all eight national annexes in one go, exactly as the installation does for the desktop
application; AD.API.Environments.DesignCodes then overrides individual ones.



SEND IT. Null does NOT mean a neutral default - it means "keep the eight standards this
MACHINE is configured for", read from the per-user Advance Design settings. The same
request then produces a Eurocode model on one machine and an ACI / AISC model on another,
and a AD.API.Environments.DesignCodes object accepted on one can be refused on the other,
because the annex rules are checked against whatever standard is in force. It is the one
property whose absence makes the result depend on the server's installation.

logVerbosity.description:
Verbosity level for engine log output in API responses. Level 1: Errors only. Level 2: Errors and Warnings. Level 3: All details. Default is ErrorsAndWarnings (2).

Possible values:

  • 1 - Errors: Level 1: Only errors are included in the API response diagnostics.
  • 2 - ErrorsAndWarnings: Level 2: Errors and warnings are included in the API response diagnostics.
  • 3 - AllDetails: Level 3: All details (errors, warnings, and informational messages) are included.

designCodes.description:
The design standards and national annexes to impose on the session, overriding what
AD.API.Environments.Localization resolves to.



Null - the default - means "take all eight from the localization", which is what every
caller got before this property existed. Deliberately NOT initialised to an empty object:
a request that does not mention design standards must not read as one that mentions them
all. Inside it, each property is null on the same terms. See
AD.API.DesignCodes.



A standard or annex combination the desktop application could not produce fails the whole
`NewProject` / `OpenProject` call, with the reason in the response diagnostics.

Environments.description:
Environment settings - the language, the localization, the diagnostics verbosity and the
design standards a session runs under.



IT CONFIGURES THE SESSION, AND A SESSION IS CONFIGURED ONCE. The environment takes effect on
the `NewProject` / `OpenProject` call that opens the session and lasts as long as
that project. A call sent while a project is still open is REFUSED - the whole call, not
just the environment: the localization and design standards were read while that model was
built and are read again by the generation and by the design Experts, so running a second
project on them would calculate it under standards it was never described with. Close the
project first; the next one takes a new environment.



THE LANGUAGE IS NARROWER STILL - fixed for the life of the SERVER PROCESS. The first
environment settles it, and the two ways of changing it afterwards are treated differently:


* an EXPLICIT AD.API.Environments.Language that disagrees with the one in force is REFUSED, and
  the caller is told to restart the server;


* a language merely IMPLIED by AD.API.Environments.Localization is HELD BACK with a warning, and
  the rest of that localization - its eight design standards, which is what it is really
  being asked for - is applied normally. Refusing here instead would tie a whole server to
  one localization family, since sixteen of the eighteen localizations imply a language
  other than English.



The restriction is what the desktop application achieves by restarting itself: reloading the
prompt database is not enough, because the catalogues, units and resources already loaded
keep the language they were read in.



WHAT IT WRITES. Everything this environment configures lives in the server's memory for the
life of the session; no design standard, annex, localization or language chosen here is
written back to the machine's Advance Design configuration. One thing is not in that
promise, and it is not this API's doing: OPENING the in-memory session seeds it by reading
the per-user registry, and Advance Design's own accessors write a default back when they
find a value missing. So on a machine where Advance Design has never run, the first request
materialises the default keys - with the values the read already resolved to, never with
anything this request named.

Eurocode2ndGenCombinationsGenerationSett.description:
Settings of the 2nd generation Eurocode (EN 1990:2023).



EXPOSED BUT NOT YET REACHABLE. The standard is still under development, and no session
localization resolves to it, so `GetModelSettings` will not return
this type and `SetModelSettings` will refuse it - the active
standard has to match. It is here so that the shape is settled and the same for all
five standards.



Two things differ from the 1st generation settings beyond the field names:

- The per-family coefficients are LISTS of rows, one per action family, matched by
`Family`. Rows the request does not name are left alone; a family the model has no
row for is refused, because the model vector cannot grow from here - building those
rows is the model creation path's job.

category-to-psi derivation still lives in the desktop options dialog, so what is sent
here is what gets stored. That is the one place where this standard is deliberately
NOT uniform with the other four, and it will change when that derivation is shared.

systemIDs.description:
Internal ids (AD.API.EID) of the systems (`som.System`) this element belongs to.
An element can belong to several systems. 

- On Get: populated with the element's current systems. 

- On Create: the element is created in the first listed system and added to the rest; when
  empty, it is placed in the model's default root system ("Structure 0"); a listed id that is not an existing system makes the creation fail. 

- On Update: when non-empty, the element's membership is set to exactly these systems (added
  to the new ones, removed from the others); when empty, the membership is left unchanged.
  Invalid system ids are rejected (the update fails without changing any membership). 

- The support always belongs to at least one system: it can never be left with none. If it
  would be (its systems were deleted, or the requested membership could not be applied), it is
  put back in the root system "Structure 0" and a warning is logged.

LicenceProtectionType.description:
The kind of licence the server runs under - the licence component's own classification, value for value. `Unknown` is the one value the licence component does not have: it stands for a number it reported that is none of the others, so a newer licence component can never make this enumeration lie by name.

Possible values:

  • 0 - NoLicence: No licence.
  • 1 - Demo: Demonstration licence.
  • 2 - Evaluation: Evaluation (trial) licence.
  • 3 - Education: Education licence.
  • 4 - Commercial: Commercial licence.
  • 5 - Reseller: Reseller licence.
  • 6 - Internal: Graitec internal licence.
  • 7 - HomeUse: Home-use licence.
  • -1 - Unknown: The licence component reported a kind this server does not know.

checkedAt.description:
When the licence was read for this snapshot.

Default value: 0001-01-01T00:00:00+00:00

isAvailable.description:
True when the server holds its MANDATORY licence - the base module and the user seat,
checked out together when the server started. Without it no model operation can be relied
upon, and AD.API.LicenceStatus.ErrorMessage says why.



The mandatory licence is checked out once, at startup, and never checked out again
afterwards: a network licence whose lease is lost later is NOT detected here.

Default value: false

errorMessage.description:
Why the mandatory licence is not held, in words a user can act on: the licence component's
own message without its technical lines (licence server names, licence file paths, raw error
codes - those go to the server log only), or, when nothing is left of it, a description of
what failed. Also set when the licence was released because the server is shutting down,
and - with AD.API.LicenceStatus.IsAvailable true - when the licence is held but its details could
not be read. `null` when there is nothing to report.

Default value: null

protectionType.description:
The kind of licence the server runs under. Default value: LicenceProtectionType.NoLicence

Possible values:

  • 0 - NoLicence: No licence.
  • 1 - Demo: Demonstration licence.
  • 2 - Evaluation: Evaluation (trial) licence.
  • 3 - Education: Education licence.
  • 4 - Commercial: Commercial licence.
  • 5 - Reseller: Reseller licence.
  • 6 - Internal: Graitec internal licence.
  • 7 - HomeUse: Home-use licence.
  • -1 - Unknown: The licence component reported a kind this server does not know.

isPermanent.description:
True when the base module's licence never expires. AD.API.LicenceStatus.DaysToExpiry is null then.

Default value: false

daysToExpiry.description:
Days left before the base module's licence expires, counted when the snapshot was taken.
`null` when the licence is permanent, when none is held, or when the licence component
could not tell.

Default value: null

designCalculations.description:
Whether each design family's licence is available. The server always fills in every
`DesignCalculationType` it knows, in the order of that enumeration.

Default value: empty (the server fills it)

LicenceStatus.description:
The licence section of `GetStatus`: whether this server holds the licence it needs to
run, and what that licence allows.



A SNAPSHOT, NOT A LIVE READ. The licence is read when the server starts, and again now and
then when the server is idle; AD.API.LicenceStatus.CheckedAt says when this one was taken. Reading it
never waits behind a running model operation.


AD.API.LicenceStatus.IsAvailable is the one value that decides whether the server can work. Everything
else describes the licence it holds, and is at its default when it holds none - including once
the licence has been RELEASED because the server is shutting down: then only
AD.API.LicenceStatus.CheckedAt and AD.API.LicenceStatus.ErrorMessage are set, and nothing of the released
licence is reported any more.

Base class of the Expert design templates that apply to LINEAR elements (beams, columns, bars) -
the templates whose AD.API.DesignTemplate.ElementType is
AD.API.DesignTemplateElementType.linear. 


This level of the hierarchy carries no property of its own: it exists so that a linear element
can refer to "a linear design template" independently of the material family and of the design
code, and so that the planar counterpart can be added later without restructuring. The design
properties are on the leaf classes, e.g. AD.API.EC3SteelLinearDesignTemplate. 


A linear element references one of these templates through
AD.API.ElementLinear.DesignTemplateId. 

Available for the descriptive model only.

LinearReleaseTemplate.description:
Linear release template (maps to the AD model object `som.LinearRelease`). 

Templates live in a single model-level pool and describe how an edge of a planar element is
connected to the rest of the structure. They are defined once and then referenced by the
edges of any number of planar elements through AD.API.ElementPlanar.LinearReleases and
AD.API.ElementPlanar.SelectedReleaseName - editing a template therefore changes every
edge that uses it. 


Every model always contains three built-in templates, in this order : 

- "Free"   : all four degrees of freedom released, 

- "Pinned" : Tx, Ty, Tz fixed and Rx released, 

- "Fixed"  : all four degrees of freedom fixed (the default for a new planar element). 

Their names are localized, so list the templates (query
`InformationalElementTypeEnum.LinearReleaseTemplate`) instead of hard-coding a name.
The three built-ins cannot be modified nor deleted through the API. 


The template name is AD.API.LinearReleaseTemplate.LinearReleaseName and it must be unique in the model; the
base-class member AD.API.InformationalElementBase.UserName is not used. 

Available for the descriptive model only.

Load_Area_Type.description:
Load area climatic type

Possible values:

  • 0 - CG_LOADAREA_BUILDING: building wall( >= GR_MIN_VERTICAL_WALL_ANGLE degrees) or roof( < GR_MIN_VERTICAL_WALL_ANGLE)
  • 1 - CG_LOADAREA_PROTRUDING_ROOF: protruding roof(avancees de toiture) ex awning(auvent) roof
  • 2 - CG_LOADAREA_PARAPET: parapet(acrotere) wall
  • 3 - CG_LOADAREA_ISOLATED_1_SLOPED_ROOF: isolated 1 sloped roof(1 slope canopy) (toiture isolee a 1 versant)
  • 4 - CG_LOADAREA_ISOLATED_2_SLOPED_ROOF: isolated 2 sloped roof(2 sloped canopy) (toiture isolee a 2 versants)
  • 5 - CG_LOADAREA_PANEL: Panel or sign
  • 6 - CG_LOADAREA_FOR_SCAFFOLDING: all the linear elements that are inside or intersecting the closed enveloppe with this type of windwalls are considered to be part of scaffolding, com tower, ...
  • 7 - CG_LOADAREA_SHED_VERTICAL_ROOF: shed vertical roof used in monopitch sheds or for 75 degrees < roofs < 80 degrees
  • 8 - CG_LOADAREA_AWNING: awning(auvent) roof
  • 9 - CG_LOADAREA_VAULTED_ROOFS_AND_DOMES: circular load area (windwall) for circular roofs, vaulted roofs, domes, ...
  • 11 - CG_LOADAREA_LOWER_ANGLE_INCLINED_WALL: 45.1 < lower angle inclined wall < GR_MIN_VERTICAL_WALL_ANGLE(75)
  • 12 - CG_LOADAREA_FREE_STANDING_WALL: free standing wall

settingsCategory.description:
Which group of model settings this object carries.



READ ONLY: it is filled by `GetModelSettings` and ignored in a
`SetModelSettings` request, where the group follows from the object's own type.
It is here so that a returned object says what it is without its `$type` having to
be parsed.



Named `SettingsCategory` and not `Category` on purpose: a group's own shapes
carry categories of their own - the live load, snow, wind and temperature
`Category` of the combination settings - and two properties called the same at two
levels of one request body is how a caller ends up sending the wrong one.

ModelSettingsBase.description:
Base class of the GENERAL SETTINGS of a model: the options that apply to the model as a
whole rather than to any one object of it, and that in the AD model live on
`som.ModelProperties`.



These are NOT properties of an element, a load case or a combination. They are what the
desktop application edits in its option dialogs - which project situations the combination
generation produces, which coefficients it applies, and, as they are added, the general
options of the Expert design calculations. They are read, written and reset through THREE
generic functions, whatever the group:

- `GetModelSettings(category)` returns the settings of one group,

- `SetModelSettings(settings)` writes them, and

- `ResetModelSettings(category)` puts back what the model's standard prescribes.



THE OBJECT DECIDES WHAT IS WRITTEN. `SetModelSettings` takes this base class, so it is
the runtime type of the object - its `$type` - that says which group of model settings
the call writes, exactly as `CreateInformationalElement` takes
AD.API.InformationalElementBase and the object decides what is created. There is no
function per group of settings, and adding a group adds no function.



TWO LEVELS OF DERIVATION. Under this base, one class per group of settings
(AD.API.CombinationsGenerationSettings, AD.API.SteelCalculationSettings and
AD.API.AiscSteelCalculationSettings today) - and under that class, as many classes as
the group has shapes. The combination generation has five, one per combination standard,
because the standards share no field; each of the two steel groups has one, because the
codes inside a family share every page of the dialog. So the class hierarchy reads: what
settings (level 2), in which variant (level 3).



TWO STEEL GROUPS, NOT ONE GROUP WITH TWO SHAPES. The Eurocode and the North-American
families do not answer the same question - the second has no Partial safety factors page at
all and a Verification page of three controls instead of thirteen - so they are separate
categories with separate group classes. The five pages they do share are the same DTO
classes, held by both group classes.



PARTIAL BY DESIGN. In every group, the properties are optional and what a request does not
carry keeps the value the model has, so a single switch can be changed without restating
the rest. What each group refuses, what it recomputes rather than stores, and what it
reports as a warning instead of an error is documented on that group's own class.

NorthAmericanSteelColdFormedDesign.description:
"Cold formed design options" group of a North-American steel design template - the AISI S100
options (maps to the AD model object `som.AISCRoleColdFormedDesign`, which derives from
`som.AISIColdFormedDesign`). 


A different object from the Eurocode AD.API.EC3SteelColdFormedDesign, and reached through
a differently named slot of the expert object ("ColdFormedDesignOptions" against the Eurocode
"RoleColdFormedDesignOptions"). 


Most of the group describes WEB CRIPPLING (AISI S100 clause G5): the bearing length and the
support conditions at the two kinds of support decide which coefficient row of the standard's
table the design engine picks.

upperFlangeLength.description:
Lateral-torsional buckling length of the UPPER flange (maps to "Lds", from the French
"longueur de deversement superieure" - the field name is shared with the French CM66 code,
whose object shape the North-American codes reuse). 


THE SAME PHYSICAL QUANTITY AS
AD.API.NorthAmericanSteelLateralTorsionalBucklingParameters.LengthValue of
AD.API.NorthAmericanSteelLateralTorsionalBucklingLength.UpperFlangeParameters - Advance Design stores it twice, and its dialog derives
this one from the other when it closes. There are therefore two ways to set it, and both work: 
send this length ALONE and the flange's mode switches to "imposed" with it, exactly as typing it
in the property list does; or send the flange's own mode and value and leave this at 0, and it
is derived - under the North-American codes it simply follows the flange's value, whatever the
mode, so it carries the length for the imposed mode and the COEFFICIENT for the computed
ones. 

Either way the 0 default is never taken literally, so an update that sends this group without
AD.API.NorthAmericanSteelLateralTorsionalBucklingLength.UpperFlangeParameters keeps the stored length. Note that SENDING that flange
group does reset the properties of the flange you leave unset, as every group does. 

Unit : m 

Default value : 0.0

"UpperFlange"). 

Output only and localized: Advance Design rebuilds this string from
AD.API.NorthAmericanSteelLateralTorsionalBucklingLength.UpperFlangeParameters (its `StartRestraint` and `EndRestraint`), so a
value sent here is overwritten. Do not parse it - read the restraints instead.

NorthAmericanSteelLateralTorsionalBuckli.description:
Lateral-torsional buckling lengths of a North-American steel design template (maps to the AD
model object `som.CM66RoleSDLateralTorsionBuckling`). 


The two flanges are treated independently, because the compressed flange is the one that needs
restraining and which flange is compressed depends on the moment sign: each has its own length
and its own parameter set. 


Compared with AD.API.EC3SteelLateralTorsionalBucklingLength there is no buckling curve:
`som.CM66RoleSDLateralTorsionBuckling` has no "LateralTorsionBucklingCurve" field, because
AISC 360 and CAN/CSA S16 derive the resistance from the unbraced length and Cb rather than from
a tabulated curve.

Default value : true

startRestraint.description:

Default value : SteelLtbEndRestraint.no_restraint

How the unbraced length of this flange is obtained (maps to "Longueur"). 

Default value : SteelBucklingLengthMode.auto_length

lengthValue.description:
Unbraced length, or the coefficient applied to the computed one (maps to
"LongueurValue"). 

It is a LENGTH in metres when AD.API.NorthAmericanSteelLateralTorsionalBucklingParameters.LengthMode is
AD.API.SteelBucklingLengthMode.imposed, and a dimensionless coefficient when the mode
derives the length from the element, the mesh size or the super-element. 

The dialog refuses an imposed value that is not strictly greater than 0, and so does the
API. 

Unit : m or adimensional, see above 

Default value : 1.0

cbMode.description:
How the Cb moment modification factor is obtained (maps to "KD"). 

Cb accounts for the shape of the moment diagram over the unbraced length - AISC 360 clause F1,
CAN/CSA S16 clause 13.6 calls the same quantity omega2. The stored field is the CM66 "kD"
slot, reused by the North-American codes. 

Default value : SteelLtbFactorCbMode.auto_cb

Used only when AD.API.NorthAmericanSteelLateralTorsionalBucklingParameters.CbMode is

Default value : 0.0

NorthAmericanSteelLateralTorsionalBuckli.description:
Lateral-torsional buckling parameters of one flange of a North-American steel design template
(maps to the AD model object `som.CM66RoleSDLateralTorsionBucklingParameters`). 


The same class is used twice, once per flange. It gathers the lateral restraints at the two ends
of the flange, the unbraced length, and the Cb moment modification factor. 


FOUR FIELDS OF THE UNDERLYING OBJECT ARE NOT EXPOSED. <c>som.CM66RoleSDLateralTorsionBuckling
Parameters</c> is shared with the French CM66 code and carries its B, C, D and PointDeCharge
coefficients as well. The AISC / CAN/CSA lateral-torsional-buckling dialog
(`CGrAmericaRoleMetalDeversementSheet`) writes none of them and the North-American design
engine reads none of them, so exposing them would only offer a caller a way to store values that
nothing consumes. The one field of that CM66 set the North-American codes DO reuse is the
kD pair, under the meaning Cb - see AD.API.NorthAmericanSteelLateralTorsionalBucklingParameters.CbMode.

"Design template description" dialog only lists it under AISC: the CAN/CSA template is missing
its resource entry, so the values sent here for a CAN/CSA template reach the design engine and

NorthAmericanSteelLinearDesignTemplate.description:
Base class of the Expert design templates for linear STEEL elements verified to a NORTH-AMERICAN
code - AISC 360 or CAN/CSA S16 (maps to the AD model objects `som.AISCSteelLinearRole` and
`som.CSASteelLinearRole`, held by `som.Role` in its "AISCSteelLinearExpertProperties"
and "CSASteelLinearExpertProperties" slots). 


WHY THE TWO CODES SHARE A BASE. Advance Design gives them two distinct SOM classes, but those two
classes differ by exactly two things: the meaning of the cross-section class, and the Class 4
effective characteristics, which only CAN/CSA carries. Everything else - the 2nd-order analysis,
the deflections, the flexural and torsional buckling, the lateral-torsional buckling, the
AISC/CSA specific properties, the cold-formed options and the angle verification - is the same
object graph, initialized by the same branch of `CRoleManager::CreateLinearMetalExpert` and
copied to the element by the same branch of `CLinearElementAccessor::ApplyRole`. That
shared part lives here; AD.API.AISCSteelLinearDesignTemplate and
AD.API.CSASteelLinearDesignTemplate only add what genuinely differs. 


This class is NOT creatable on its own: a template always belongs to one of the two codes, so
Create and Update require one of the two leaves. Sending this base is refused. 


HOW IT DIFFERS FROM THE EUROCODE LEAF. Compared with
AD.API.EC3SteelLinearDesignTemplate, the North-American templates have NO manufacturing
quality, NO execution class, NO family of element, NO global sway imperfections, NO fire
verification and NO web-buckling group - Advance Design does not allocate those sub-objects
outside the Eurocode. They gain
AD.API.NorthAmericanSteelLinearDesignTemplate.SteelSpecificProperties (the HSS design
thickness, the Kt factor, the web stiffeners and the double-angle connector spacing) and a
simpler lateral-torsional-buckling group built around the Cb moment modification factor instead
of the Eurocode C1/C2/C3 coefficients. 


PARTIAL UPDATE - every group below is nullable. On Update, a group left null keeps its stored
value, so a caller can patch one group without restating the rest. Lists inside a group are the
exception: when a list is sent it replaces the stored one in full. 

Available for the descriptive model only.

NorthAmericanSteelSpecificProperties.description:
"Steel specific properties" group of a North-American steel design template (maps to the AD

AISC and AD.API.NorthAmericanSteelSpecificProperties.CheckForTorsionAndShear under anything but CAN/CSA. Sending a

so a payload can never store a value the desktop could not have produced; use a

- On Create / Update: optional. Entries beyond the number of segments are ignored, and the
  segments the list does not cover keep their current values - so a shorter list sets only
  the first segments. A warning is logged when the count does not match. A null entry is
  skipped the same way: that segment keeps its current values.

- When an Update changes AD.API.ElementPolyLine.GeomPtsList, the vector is resized to
  the new number of segments FIRST (new segments get the Advance Design defaults, extra ones
  are dropped), then the list sent in the SAME update is applied on top of it.

fe.description:
Elastic (Euler) critical buckling stress Fe, in N/m^2. AISC 360 equation (E3-4).
Native: df_Fe.

NULL UNDER EVERY CSA S16 CODE, and the reason is a unit defect in the writer rather than a
missing quantity. The engine DOES compute it on the CSA branch - verified as exactly
pi^2 E / (KL/r)^2 with E = 200 GPa, to all reported digits, on two different members - but the
CSA branch stores it WITHOUT the conversion its AISC sibling applies: the AISC path writes
`KSI_TO_PA(df_Fe)` and the CSA path writes `df_Fe` unchanged
(`GrMetalSolverManagerAISC.cpp:8219` against `:8225`). The struct therefore holds
MEGApascals in a field this property declares as pascals - 3308.4 where 3.3084e9 is meant, a
factor of a million.
Reported as null rather than converted here on purpose, and FIXING THE WRITER WOULD NOT BY ITSELF
make it safe to report. The value is persisted into the result file, so after such a fix a model
calculated before it still holds MPa and one calculated after holds Pa, with nothing in the file
to tell the two apart - a reader would have to guess, and guessing wrong is a factor of a million.
Re-enabling this property therefore needs the writer corrected AND something that distinguishes
the two vintages, such as a result-file version. Rescaling in the mapper instead would be worse
still: it would be silently wrong for every model calculated after the writer is fixed.
Note that only this API reads the field under CSA - Advance Design's own Canadian shape sheet
never prints Fe (GrTableExpertMetalProfileInfoCA.cpp does not reference it), which is why the
defect went unnoticed. So nothing in the application depends on the current MPa value either.

fcr.description:
Critical stress Fcr, in N/m^2 - Fe reduced for inelastic buckling by equation (E3-2) or (E3-3).
Native: df_Fcr.

NULL UNDER EVERY CSA S16 CODE, this one because the quantity does not exist there: clause 13.3.1
goes from the non-dimensional slenderness straight to the factored resistance Cr, with no
intermediate critical stress, so the CSA branch leaves the field at zero. A reported 0.0 Pa would
read as a real, and alarming, answer.

pn.description:
NOMINAL compressive strength Pn = Fcr * Ag, in N. Note this is the nominal value, NOT reduced by
phi or Omega - the reduced one is AD.API.ResAiscResistanceCheck.Strength of the axial
check. Native: df_Pn.

ResAiscAxialCompressionDetail.description:
The quantities behind the axial COMPRESSION strength of AISC 360 chapter E / CSA S16 clause 13.3.
Native: the df_KLr / df_Fe / df_Fcr / df_Pn fields of aisc_Resistance.

lfy.description:
Buckling length about y-y, in m - the KL of AISC 360 chapter E and CSA S16 clause 13.3.
Native: dfLfy.

lfz.description: Buckling length about z-z, in m. Native: dfLfz.

lfyOverSuperElementLength.description:
Ratio of a buckling length to the length of the super element, as the engine stores it in the
field named for y-y. Native: dfLfyOnLSElt.

lfzOverSuperElementLength.description:
The companion ratio, as stored in the field named for z-z. See
AD.API.ResAiscBucklingLengths.LfyOverSuperElementLength. Native: dfLfzOnLSElt.

slendernessLfy.description:
Slenderness ratio KL/r for buckling about y-y, dimensionless. Native: dfSlendernessLfy. A value
above 200 is what raises AD.API.AiscResistanceWarning.SlendernessRatioAbove200 on the
axial check.

slendernessLfz.description: Slenderness ratio KL/r for buckling about z-z, dimensionless. Native: dfSlendernessLfz.

ResAiscBucklingLengths.description: Flexural buckling lengths and the slendernesses derived from them. Native: aisc_Buckling.

loadingPattern.description: Which stress pattern this classification was performed against.

aiscSectionClass.description:
Class of the cross-section as a whole under this pattern, AISC 360. Set only under an AISC
edition. Native: iClass_* holding an AISC_CROSS_SECTION_CLASS. The native default is -1, meaning
the pattern was not classified, which is reported as AD.API.AiscCrossSectionClass.Unknown.

csaSectionClass.description:
Class of the cross-section as a whole under this pattern, CSA S16. Set only under a CSA edition.
Native: the same iClass_* field, holding a CSA_CROSS_SECTION_CLASS.

parts.description:
Per-plate classification under this pattern, as many entries as the section has parts.
Native: iPartType_* and iPartClass*.

ResAiscClassPerLoadingPattern.description: The classification of the cross-section against one stress pattern.

mrz.description: Required flexural strength about z-z, Mrz, in N*m. Native: df_Mrz.

mcy.description: Available flexural strength about y-y, Mcy, in N*m. Native: df_Mcy.

mcz.description: Available flexural strength about z-z, Mcz, in N*m. Native: df_Mcz.

vry.description: Required shear strength along y, Vry, in N. Native: df_Vry.

vcy.description: Available shear strength along y, Vcy, in N. Native: df_Vcy.

vrz.description: Required shear strength along z, Vrz, in N. Native: df_Vrz.

vcz.description: Available shear strength along z, Vcz, in N. Native: df_Vcz.

tr.description: Required torsional strength Tr, in N*m. Native: df_Tr.

tc.description: Available torsional strength Tc, in N*m. Native: df_Tc.

beta.description:
The interaction exponent beta, dimensionless - CSA S16 clause 13.8's beta, and the equivalent

Second-order amplification factor U1 for bending about y-y, dimensionless - CSA S16 clause 13.8.

u1z.description:
Second-order amplification factor U1 for bending about z-z, dimensionless.

Available compressive strength OUT OF THE PLANE OF BENDING, Pcy, in N. Used by the alternative

Available lateral-torsional strength for strong-axis flexure, in N*m. The companion of
AD.API.ResAiscCombinedForcesDetail.Pcy in AISC 360 equation (H1-2). Native: df_McLTB.

ResAiscCombinedForcesDetail.description:
The quantities behind the combined-forces interaction, AISC 360 chapter H / CSA S16 clauses 13.8
and 13.9. Native: the df_Pr ... df_McLTB fields of aisc_Resistance.

isImposed.description:
True when the user forced the class on the design template instead of letting the engine compute

classification.

classPerLoadingPattern.description:
Classification per stress pattern - four entries, one per member of
AD.API.AiscClassLoadingPattern.

ResAiscCrossSectionClass.description: Cross-section classification under a North American code. Native: aisc_Class.

elementVerificationLocation.description:
Where the ELEMENT-level deflection was required to be verified, as set on the design template.

superElementVerificationLocation.description:
Where the SUPER-ELEMENT-level deflection was required to be verified, as set on the design
template. Native: iLocation_SE.

superElementEnd.description:
Deflection at the extremity of the super element - the absolute displacement of its ends.
Native: the *_SEExtremity fields.

superElementSpan.description:
Deflection in the span of the super element, relative to the line joining its ends.
Native: the *_SESpan fields.

segmentSpan.description:
Deflection in the span of one segment, relative to the line joining that segment's ends.
Native: the *_TronSpan fields.

segmentEnd.description:
Deflection at the end of one segment, relative to that segment's start.
Native: the *_TronEnd fields.

envelope.description:
The governing location, whichever of the above the verification settings selected.
Native: the *_Envelope fields.

superElementLength.description: Reference length the super-element locations were divided by, in m. Native: df_Length_SE.

segmentLength.description: Reference length the segment locations were divided by, in m. Native: df_Length_Tron.

envelopeLength.description: Reference length the envelope location was divided by, in m. Native: df_Length_Envelope.

allowableCoefficient.description:
Allowable deflection of an ELEMENT, as the denominator of L/x - the design template's L/360 is
reported as 360. Native: df_All_Coeff.

allowableCoefficientSuperElement.description:
Allowable deflection of a SUPER ELEMENT, as the denominator of L/x.
Native: df_All_Coeff_SuperElem.

ResAiscDeflection.description:
Deflections of one element against one allowable-deflection criterion, at every location the engine
measured. Native: aisc_Deflection.

exists.description:
True when a deflection was found at this location. When false the numbers below are meaningless -
they are the struct's initialisers, not a deflection of zero. Native: bExist_*.

caseNumber.description:
Index of the most unfavourable load combination, as the engine stores it - the raw engine index,
not an EID and not a user combination number. Native: iCase_*.

nodeNumber.description: Node the extreme deflection was found at. Native: iNode_*.

deflectionValue.description: The deflection itself, in m. Native: df_Defl_Val_*.

effectiveCoefficient.description:
The deflection expressed as the denominator of Length/x - a deflection of L/360 is reported as
360. Note it moves OPPOSITE to severity: a larger value is a smaller deflection.
Native: df_Eff_Coeff_*.

workRatio.description:
Work ratio, dimensionless. Above 1 means the allowable deflection is exceeded. Not multiplied by
100. Native: df_WR_*.

ResAiscDeflectionLocationResult.description: The deflection found at one measurement location, for one allowable-deflection criterion.

lp.description:
Limiting unbraced length for the plastic moment, Lp, in m. AISC 360 equation (F2-5).
Native: dfLp*.

lr.description:
Limiting unbraced length for inelastic lateral-torsional buckling, Lr, in m. AISC 360 equation
(F2-6). Native: dfLr*.

lb.description:
Actual unbraced length Lb, in m, for the combination that governed this check - the same quantity
AD.API.ResAiscLateralTorsionalBucklingLengths reports per flange along the whole member.
Native: dfLb*.

cb.description:
Lateral-torsional buckling modification factor Cb, dimensionless - the allowance for a
non-uniform moment diagram, AISC 360 equation (F1-1). Native: dfCb*.

fcr.description: Critical stress Fcr for lateral-torsional buckling, in N/m^2. Native: dfFcr*.

mn.description:
NOMINAL flexural strength Mn, in N*m - the governing (smallest) of the applicable limit states.
Not reduced by phi or Omega; the reduced value is
AD.API.ResAiscResistanceCheck.Strength of the corresponding bending check.
Native: dfMn*.

mn_Yielding.description:
Nominal flexural strength for the YIELDING limit state, in N*m. Major axis and AISC 360 only;
see the note above. Native: df_Mny_Y.

mn_LateralTorsionalBuckling.description:
Nominal flexural strength for the LATERAL-TORSIONAL BUCKLING limit state, in N*m. Major axis and
AISC 360 only. Native: df_Mny_LTB.

mn_FlangeLocalBuckling.description:
Nominal flexural strength for the FLANGE LOCAL BUCKLING limit state, in N*m. Major axis and
AISC 360 only. Native: df_Mny_FLB.

mn_TensionFlangeYielding.description:
Nominal flexural strength for the TENSION FLANGE YIELDING limit state, in N*m. Major axis and
AISC 360 only. Native: df_Mny_TFY.

mn_LocalBuckling.description:
Nominal flexural strength for the WEB LOCAL BUCKLING limit state - or, for the shapes where that
is what applies, local buckling or leg local buckling - in N*m. Major axis and AISC 360 only.
Native: df_Mny_LB.

ResAiscFlexuralDetail.description:
The quantities behind one flexural strength, AISC 360 chapter F / CSA S16 clauses 13.5 and 13.6.
Native: the dfLp* / dfLr* / dfLb* / dfCb* / dfFcr* / dfMn* fields of aisc_Resistance.

lbi.description: Unbraced length for the inferior flange, in m. Native: dfLbi.

lbs.description: Unbraced length for the superior flange, in m. Native: dfLbs.

lbiOverSuperElementLength.description: Ratio of Lbi to the length of the super element. Native: dfLbiOnLSElt.

lbsOverSuperElementLength.description: Ratio of Lbs to the length of the super element. Native: dfLbsOnLSElt.

slendernessLbi.description: Slenderness associated with Lbi, dimensionless. Native: dfSlendernessLbi.

slendernessLbs.description: Slenderness associated with Lbs, dimensionless. Native: dfSlendernessLbs.

ResAiscLateralTorsionalBucklingLengths.description:
Lateral-torsional buckling (unbraced) lengths and slendernesses.
Native: aisc_TorsionalBuckling.

workRatios.description:
The available maxima, at most one entry per component. Families the accessor cannot answer for
are absent from the list rather than reported as zero, so that "not checked" and "checked, ratio
0" stay distinguishable.

ResAiscMaxWorkRatio.description:
The governing work ratio of the element and the per-family maxima behind it, under a North American
code.

designMethod.description:
Whether the strengths reported below are LRFD design values or ASD allowable values, under an
AISC 360 code. Native: iMethod. See AD.API.AiscDesignMethod - it changes what
AD.API.ResAiscResistanceCheck.Strength means, so read it before comparing a strength
against anything.

NULL UNDER EVERY CSA S16 CODE, because the question does not apply there and the native field
cannot be trusted to say so. CSA S16 is limit-states design only - it has no allowable-strength
format - but iMethod is filled from the model-wide AISC method setting
(`DefaultValues::GetAISCMethod()`, ASD by default) whatever code the model runs, so a
Canadian result would otherwise claim "ASD". That would be wrong twice over: the S16 routines
force LRFD for the duration of the computation and then RESTORE the setting
(FTEngineAISC S16_Flexure.cpp:1173 and S16_Torsion.cpp:54), so not even the computation used the
value that ends up in the struct. Reported as null for the same reason
`ResAiscFlexuralDetail.Mn_Yielding` and the CSA side of the formula pairing are: a field the
engine leaves meaningless must not be handed to a caller as if it meant something.

isCompression.description:
True when the governing axial force was compression, so the axial check is chapter E / clause
13.3 and AD.API.ResAiscResistance.AxialDetail is meaningful. False when it was tension - chapter D / clause
13.2, which has no buckling term. Native: bIsCompression.

checks.description:
The seven checks, one per member of AD.API.AiscResistanceCheckId. Checks the engine did
not perform are present with AD.API.ResAiscResistanceCheck.IsCalculated false, so that
"not checked" stays distinguishable from "checked, utilisation nil".

axialDetail.description:
Buckling quantities behind the axial check. Meaningful only when
AD.API.ResAiscResistance.IsCompression is true.

bendingYYDetail.description: Quantities behind the bending-about-y-y check, including its lateral-torsional buckling terms.

bendingZZDetail.description:
Quantities behind the bending-about-z-z check. Its five per-limit-state strengths are ALWAYS
null: the native struct records that breakdown for the major axis only, having no df_Mnz_*
counterpart to its five df_Mny_* fields.

combinedForcesDetail.description: Required and available strengths of every component of the combined-forces interaction.

ResAiscResistance.description: Cross-section resistance checks under a North American code. Native: aisc_Resistance.

check.description: Which check this is - the suffix of the native field group.

caseNumber.description:
Index of the most unfavourable load combination FOR THIS CHECK, as the engine stores it. Each
check keeps its own, so different checks of the same mesh cell normally report different
combinations. -1 when the check was not performed. Native: iCaseNumber*.

meshPoint.description:
Abscissa within the mesh cell where the extreme occurred, as an index in the range 0 to 4 - the
cell is sampled at its start, quarter points, mid-point and end. -1 when not recorded.
Native: iMeshPoint*.

action.description:
The acting (required) strength - a force in N or a moment in N*m depending on
AD.API.ResAiscResistanceCheck.Check. Native: df_Action*.

strength.description:
The AVAILABLE strength, in the same unit as AD.API.ResAiscResistanceCheck.Action. What "available" means depends
on AD.API.ResAiscResistance.DesignMethod: it is phi * Rn under LRFD and Rn / Omega under
ASD, the engine having applied the factor before storing it. Native: df_Strength*.

workRatio.description:
Work ratio, dimensionless. Above 1 means the check is not satisfied. Not multiplied by 100.
Native: df_WorkRatio*.

error.description: Whether the engine performed this check, and if not, why not. Native: iError*.

warning.description:
A note the engine attached to the check. Does NOT invalidate the numbers above - the check ran.
Native: iWarning*.

isCalculated.description:
True when the engine actually performed this check, so the numbers above are a result rather than
four zeros. Equivalent to AD.API.ResAiscResistanceCheck.Error being AD.API.AiscResistanceError.None, and
reported alongside it so that a client can treat a North American and a Eurocode check the same
way without knowing which flag each carries.

appliedAiscFormula.description:
The AISC 360 equation the check applied. Set only when
AD.API.ResNorthAmericaSteelLinearDesignData.DesignCode is an AISC edition; null under
CSA S16, where AD.API.ResAiscResistanceCheck.AppliedCsaFormula carries it instead. Native: iFormula* holding a
FORMULA_* value.

appliedCsaFormula.description:
The CSA S16 clause the check applied. Set only when
AD.API.ResNorthAmericaSteelLinearDesignData.DesignCode is a CSA edition; null under
AISC 360. Native: the same iFormula* field, holding a CSA_FORMULA_* value.

ResAiscResistanceCheck.description: One cross-section resistance check. Native: one of the seven eight-field blocks of aisc_Resistance.

isHaunch.description:
True when this mesh cell falls inside a haunch, in which case the properties below are the
haunch's at that position rather than the running section's. Native: bIsHaunch.

h.description: Overall depth d, m. Native: df_h.

b.description: Overall breadth b, m. Native: df_b.

tw.description: Web thickness tw, m. Native: df_tw.

tf.description: Flange thickness tf, m. Native: df_tf.

d.description: Depth of the web h, m. Native: df_d.

grossArea.description: Total cross-sectional area A, m2. Native: df_Sx.

flangeArea.description: Flange area Af, m2. Native: df_Sy.

webArea.description: Web area Aw - overall depth times web thickness, m2. Native: df_Sz.

wel1y.description: Elastic section modulus S1x about the major axis, m3. Native: df_Wel1y.

wel2y.description: Elastic section modulus S2x about the major axis, m3. Native: df_Wel2y.

wel1z.description: Elastic section modulus S1y about the minor axis, m3. Native: df_Wel1z.

wel2z.description: Elastic section modulus S2y about the minor axis, m3. Native: df_Wel2z.

wply.description: Plastic section modulus Zx about the major axis, m3. Native: df_Wply.

wplz.description: Plastic section modulus Zy about the minor axis, m3. Native: df_Wplz.

iy.description: Second moment of area Ix about the major axis, m4. Native: df_Iy.

iz.description: Second moment of area Iy about the minor axis, m4. Native: df_Iz.

it.description: Torsional constant J, m4. Native: df_Ix - NOT a second moment of area.

iw.description: Warping constant Cw, m6. Native: df_Iw.

ry.description: Radius of gyration rx about the major axis, m. Native: df_ry.

rz.description: Radius of gyration ry about the minor axis, m. Native: df_rz.

shearCentreY.description: Shear centre x0, relative to the centroid, m. Native: df_y0.

shearCentreZ.description: Shear centre y0, relative to the centroid, m. Native: df_z0.

ResAiscSectionInfo.description:
The cross-section the element was verified with at one mesh cell: its dimensions and its gross
section properties. Native: aisc_Section.

partIndex.description: Zero-based index of the part within the cross-section, in the order the engine split it.

partType.description: Role this plate plays in the classification. Native: iPartType_*.

aiscPartClass.description:
Class of this plate on its own under AISC 360. Set only when
AD.API.ResNorthAmericaSteelLinearDesignData.DesignCode is an AISC edition; null under
CSA S16, where AD.API.ResAiscSectionPart.CsaPartClass carries it instead. Native: iPartClass* holding an
AISC_CROSS_SECTION_CLASS.

csaPartClass.description:
Class of this plate on its own under CSA S16. Set only when
AD.API.ResNorthAmericaSteelLinearDesignData.DesignCode is a CSA edition; null under
AISC 360. Native: the same iPartClass* field, holding a CSA_CROSS_SECTION_CLASS.

ResAiscSectionPart.description: Classification of one plate ("part") of the cross-section, under one stress pattern.

phi_v.description:
Resistance factor phi,v for shear - used under LRFD, 0.9 or 1.0 in AISC 360 chapter G.

Safety factor Omega,v for shear - used under ASD, 1.67 or 1.50 in AISC 360 chapter G.

data.description:

May be `null` or default when AD.API.Srv.Models.ApiResponseDetails.Success is `false`.

Standard envelope returned by every API operation.
Wraps the actual result together with structured diagnostics
(errors, warnings, informational messages) so that callers –
including AI agents – can programmatically inspect the outcome.

Identifier of the load combination or case, as shown in the Advance Design interface - the same
number the analysis is created and reported under. -1 when the engine recorded none.

type depends on the requested result type.

be shorter than the element's mesh - check AD.API.ResDesignMesh.MeshIndex rather than
assuming a position.

Result family these results were requested as. When a query asked for

userID.description:

redundant with the "$type" of the payloads below and is reported for convenience.

omitted from the response rather than returned with an empty list.

userID.description:

SeismicDesignCode.description:
The seismic standard of the session. Mirrors `REG_SEISMIC_CODE_*`. Set through `Environments.DesignCodes.Seismic`; left null it stays whatever the session localization resolved to. EN 1998-1 is the only value that takes a national annex.

Possible values:

  • 4 - ps92: PS92 (original edition). Macro
  • 5 - rpa99_2003: RPA99 (2003 revision) - the Algerian seismic standard.
  • 6 - p100_1_2013: P100-1/2013 - the current Romanian seismic standard.
  • 7 - ntc2008: NTC 2008 - the Italian seismic standard, 2008 edition.
  • 8 - cnb2005: CNB 2005 - the Canadian national building code, 2005 edition. Macro
  • 9 - ibc2012: IBC 2012 - the US international building code, 2012 edition.
  • 10 - cnb2015: CNB 2015 - the Canadian national building code, 2015 edition. Macro
  • 11 - ntc2018: NTC 2018 - the current Italian seismic standard.
  • 12 - ibc2018: IBC 2018 - the US international building code, 2018 edition.
  • 13 - cnb2020: CNB 2020 - the current Canadian national building code. Macro

SteelAngleVerification.description:
"Angle verification" group of a steel design template (maps to the AD model object
`som.RoleAngleVerification`). 


Applies to angle (L) sections connected through one leg only, where the eccentricity of the
connection and the reduced net area have to be accounted for. 


NOTE on the underlying model: the field of the design template that holds this object is declared
with the type `som.AngleVerification`, but the object Advance Design actually creates is a
`som.RoleAngleVerification`. The two classes have identical field sets; this DTO follows the
class that is really instantiated.

SteelAngleVerificationSettings.description:
The Angle verification page: the bolt geometry used to compute the net area of angle
sections.



All three are MULTIPLES OF THE BOLT HOLE DIAMETER d0, not lengths, so they carry no unit.
The minima are the ones the dialog enforces and come from EN 1993-1-8 table 3.3.



Shared by both steel code families. The page carries no steel-code branch, so the same
minima are enforced under a North-American code - that is what the dialog does, and the API
must be neither stricter nor laxer than it.
