SteelBucklingLength.description:
Buckling lengths of a steel design template (maps to the AD model object
`som.RoleSDBuckling`). 


The properties come in families. For each of the two principal planes (y and z) there is a
buckling length (`Lfy` / `Lfz`), an equivalent length used for the FIRE situation
(`LfyFire` / `LfzFire`), the system length `L0`, the mu coefficient, the
braced/unbraced nature of the nodes and the equivalent uniform moment factor Cm,0. Each of these
is a mode + value (+ coefficient) triplet: the value is only used when the mode says "imposed",
and the coefficient multiplies the resulting length. On top of that come the two flexural
buckling curves and the torsional buckling length Lcr,T. 


In Advance Design only AD.API.SteelBucklingLength.Lfy, AD.API.SteelBucklingLength.Lfz, AD.API.SteelBucklingLength.YNodesType,
AD.API.SteelBucklingLength.ZNodesType and AD.API.SteelBucklingLength.TorsionalBucklingVerification appear directly in the
design-template property list; everything else is edited through the "Buckling length" button,
which opens a dedicated dialog. All of them are exposed here.

SteelBucklingLengthMode.description:
How a buckling length is obtained

Possible values:

  • 0 - auto_length: The length is determined automatically by the design engine. Default.
  • 1 - imposed: The length is imposed by the user through the companion value property.
  • 2 - calculated_from_element: The length is computed from the length of the structural element.
  • 3 - calculated_from_mesh_size: The length is computed from the finite-element mesh size.
  • 4 - calculated_from_super_element: The length is computed from the length of the super-element the element belongs to.
  • 5 - lateral_torsional_buckling_length_upper_flange: The length is taken equal to the lateral-torsional-buckling length of the upper flange.
  • 6 - lateral_torsional_buckling_length_lower_flange: The length is taken equal to the lateral-torsional-buckling length of the lower flange.

SteelBucklingMuMode.description:
How the mu buckling coefficient is obtained

Possible values:

  • 0 - auto_mu: The mu buckling coefficient is determined automatically by the design engine. Default.
  • 1 - imposed_mu: The mu buckling coefficient is imposed by the user through the companion value property.

SteelBucklingNodesType.description:
Whether the structure is braced or unbraced in a buckling plane

Possible values:

  • 0 - braced: The structure is braced in this plane: the nodes are held against lateral displacement, so the buckling length is at most the element length.
  • 1 - unbraced: The structure is unbraced (sway) in this plane: the nodes can displace laterally, so the buckling length may exceed the element length. Default for the Eurocode.

method.description:
The buckling length method. The dialog enables exactly one set of radio buttons per
steel design code, and a request naming a method the model's own code does not offer is
REFUSED:



THE EUROCODE FAMILY - `eMethodBucklingKa_Kb` and `eMethodBucklingN1_N2`;
`eMethodBucklingN1_N2` by default.


THE NORTH-AMERICAN FAMILY (AISC 360, AISC 360-16, the CAN/CSA S16 editions) -
`eMethodBucklingGa_Gb` alone, which is therefore also its default.



ECHOING BACK THE STORED VALUE IS ALWAYS ALLOWED, even when the active code does not
offer it. A model converted from another code, or an old file, can carry a method its
present code has no radio button for; refusing to write it back would make a
`GetModelSettings` then `SetModelSettings` round trip fail on such a model.
Only CHANGING the method has to land on one the code offers.

SteelBucklingSettings.description:
The Buckling page: how the automatic buckling lengths are computed.



The page's "detect intersections along a super element" checkbox is NOT here: it is an
application preference stored in the registry, not a model setting. Its per-element
equivalent is `DetectIntersectionsSuperElementY` / `...Z` on the EC3 design
template. Neither are the "type of structure" combo boxes, which CM66 alone offers.



Shared by both steel code families - it is the same page - but it is the single place where
the accepted VALUES depend on the model's steel code. See AD.API.SteelBucklingSettings.Method.

SteelCFDFlangeCondition.description:
Stiffening of the flange of a cold-formed member at the support

Possible values:

  • 0 - stiffened_or_partially_stiffened: The flange is stiffened or partially stiffened (it carries an edge stiffener). Default.
  • 1 - unstiffened: The flange is unstiffened.

SteelCFDFlangeLoadingType.description:
How many flanges the concentrated load or reaction acts on

Possible values:

  • 0 - one_flange_loading_or_reaction: One-flange loading or reaction: the clear distance to the nearest other concentrated load is at least 1.5 times the web depth. Default.
  • 1 - two_flange_loading_or_reaction: Two-flange loading or reaction: an opposed load is closer than 1.5 times the web depth, so both flanges are loaded over the same length of web.

SteelCFDSupportCondition.description:
Whether a cold-formed member is fastened to the support

Possible values:

  • 0 - fastened: The member is fastened to the support. Default.
  • 1 - unfastened: The member simply bears on the support without being fastened to it.

verify.description: Verify the elements. On by default.

calculateBuckling.description: Compute the buckling lengths. On by default.

verifyDeflections.description: Verify the deflections. On by default.

calculateShapes.description: Run the shape (section optimisation) calculation. On by default.

chainedOptimization.description:
Repeat the whole sequence until it settles, up to
AD.API.SteelCalculationSequenceSettings.CompleteCalculationCount times. Off by default.



ON A EUROCODE MODEL it is meant to be mutually exclusive with
AD.API.Ec3SteelVerificationSettings.GlobalSwayImperfections: the dialog clears one
when the other is ticked. Enabling both is WARNED, not refused - the dialog's own
enforcement acts on a hidden control that is never saved, so a desktop user can leave
both flags on and this API must be able to express the same model. Under a
North-American code there is no global sway imperfection, so nothing is reported.

completeCalculationCount.description:
How many complete calculations a chained optimisation may run. Between 1 and 20; 1 by
default. Read only when AD.API.SteelCalculationSequenceSettings.ChainedOptimization is on, and reported as a
warning when sent while it is off.

SteelCalculationSequenceSettings.description:
The Calculation sequence page: which steps a steel design run performs, in order.



Turning a step off is how a caller keeps a run short - a verification-only run, for
instance - and it is also what makes the corresponding result families come back empty from
`GetDesignResults`.



Shared by both steel code families.

designCode.description:
The steel design code the model is configured with. READ ONLY HERE - a value sent in a
`SetModelSettings` request is ignored. What decides which settings a request writes
is its `$type`, not this.



It is chosen once, for the session, with `Environments.DesignCodes.Steel` on
`NewProject` / `OpenProject`, and comes from the localization when that is
left null.



The `SecondGeneration` sub-objects below are honoured only under the 2nd generation
Eurocode 3. That standard is not released: this enumeration has no value for it, so it
cannot be asked for here, and on an installation that does not have it enabled a model
carrying it is refused by this very reader - which makes those sub-objects inert, and a
value sent in one is dropped with a warning. They are kept so the shape does not change
under existing callers when the standard does ship.

SteelCalculationSettings.description:
The general settings of the Expert STEEL design calculation, as they are stored on the
model - the same ones the Calculation Settings dialog of the desktop application edits.



These are NOT properties of any element: they are general options that apply to the whole
model and are read by the design engine, so they are set once, before calling
`LaunchDesignCalculation`. What an individual member contributes on its own - its
buckling lengths, its lateral torsional buckling data, its deflection limits - lives on
that element or on the design template assigned to it.



ONE GROUP OF MODEL SETTINGS. This class is the `SteelEc3Calculation` group of
AD.API.ModelSettingsBase, so it is read with
`GetModelSettings(eModelSettingsCategory.SteelEc3Calculation)`, written with
`SetModelSettings`, which takes the base class and takes the group from this object's
own type, and put back to what the model's steel code prescribes with
`ResetModelSettings(eModelSettingsCategory.SteelEc3Calculation)`.



THE EUROCODE FAMILY ONLY. A model designed to a North-American code has its own group,
AD.API.AiscSteelCalculationSettings / `eModelSettingsCategory.SteelAiscCalculation`,
because the dialog shows it a different set of tabs - no Partial safety factors at all, and
a Verification tab reduced to three controls. Asking for the wrong one is refused with a
message naming the right one. The five pages the two families do share are the very same
DTO classes, reused by both.



ONE SHAPE, AND A SECOND GENERATION BEHIND A GATE. The two generations of Eurocode 3 share
every page of the dialog and differ by exactly three stored values, which is why those three
live in `SecondGeneration` sub-objects of the pages they belong to rather than in a
derived class - see AD.API.Ec3SteelVerificationSettings.SecondGeneration and
AD.API.Ec3SteelSafetyFactorSettings.SecondGeneration.



EN 1993-1-1:2023 is not released. On an installation that does not have it enabled - which is
every ordinary one - a model configured with it is REFUSED by this group rather than answered
under the 1st generation, and those three sub-objects are therefore inert: a value sent in one
is dropped with a warning. On an installation that does have it, the same group serves it and
the three become live. Nothing about the shape changes either way, which is the point of
keeping them here.



HOW THE STEEL CODE IS CHOSEN. It is not part of these settings. It is resolved from the
session localization passed to `SetEnvironment` and is fixed for the life of the
project. Only the Eurocode family - Eurocode 3, NTC 2008 and NTC 2018 - has these settings at
all; under any other steel code the group is refused rather than answered with values no
engine would read. A model configured with the 2nd generation Eurocode 3 is refused on any
installation that does not have that standard enabled - it is not released, and answering it
under the 1st generation would be a wrong answer that looks like a right one.



WHEN TO CALL IT. Before `LaunchAnalysis`. These values are written to the descriptive
model, and the analysis model - which is what the design engine runs on - copies them while
it is built. Writing them after the analysis model exists leaves that copy behind until the
model is rebuilt.



WHY THE ENUMERATOR NAMES LOOK LIKE THAT. `eTypeDeCalculTractionCompression`,
`eMethodBucklingN1_N2`, `eProfileOptimizationOrderedByWeight` - every enumeration
these settings use is declared from a single shared body that the desktop application, the
design engines and this contract all include (Components\Common\EnumContents). One list of
values means the API cannot drift from the dialog, and the price of that is Advance
Design's own spellings rather than prettified ones: renaming a member here would mean
renaming it in the engine and the report generator too. The VALUES are what the model
stores, so they are stable.

Each group matches one design calculation and is relevant only when the combination lists it:
AD.API.eCombinationDesignCalculation.SteelProfiles,
AD.API.eCombinationDesignCalculation.SteelDeflections,
AD.API.eCombinationDesignCalculation.SteelConnections and
AD.API.eCombinationDesignCalculation.SteelFire. 

A group left null is filled with default values when the matching calculation is listed and the
combination does not carry the values yet; a warning is then reported in the response
diagnostics.

allowableDeflection1.description:
Denominator n of the first allowable deflection L/n (maps to "Deflection1"). 

Displayed as "Allowable defl. 1 = L/". Valid range 0..10000. 

Default value : 500

allowableDeflection2.description:

Displayed as "Allowable defl. 2 = L/". Valid range 0..10000.

Displayed as "Reference length".

Displayed as "L". Only used when AD.API.SteelDeflection.ReferenceLengthOption is

Unit : m

Displayed as "Verif. Location".

SteelDeflection.description:
Deflection limits of a steel design template, applied to the element (maps to the AD model
object `som.RoleDeflection`).

SteelDeflectionLocation.description:
Where along the element the deflection is verified

Possible values:

  • 0 - extremity: The deflection is verified at the extremities of the element only.
  • 1 - span: The deflection is verified in the span of the element only.
  • 2 - envelope: The deflection is verified over the whole element, taking the envelope of the extremity and span values. Default.

SteelDeflectionReferenceLengthOption.description:
How the reference length L of a deflection check is obtained

Possible values:

  • 0 - aligned: The reference length L is computed automatically as the aligned (chord) length of the element. Displayed as "Aligned" in Advance Design. Default.
  • 1 - imposed: The reference length L is imposed by the user. This is the only option for which the reference length value is editable.
  • 2 - projected: The reference length L is computed automatically as the projected length of the element.

SteelDesignCode.description:
Steel design code configured on the model

Possible values:

  • 1 - eurocode: Eurocode 3 - EN 1993 (1st generation). Uses the EC3 expert property set.
  • 2 - aisc: AISC 360 (the edition Advance Design has always called simply AISC). The steel code of
  • 3 - can_csa_s16_2009: CAN/CSA S16-09 - the 2009 edition of the Canadian steel standard.
  • 4 - ntc2008: NTC 2008 - the Italian national application of Eurocode 3. Uses the EC3 expert property set; it differs from
  • 5 - can_csa_s16_2014: CAN/CSA S16-14 - the 2014 edition of the Canadian steel standard.
  • 6 - ntc2018: NTC 2018 - the current Italian national application of Eurocode 3. Uses the EC3 expert property set.
  • 7 - aisc_2016: AISC 360-16. The steel code of
  • 8 - can_csa_s16_2019: CAN/CSA S16-19. The steel code of
  • 10 - can_csa_s16_2024: CAN/CSA S16-24. A distinct model value, but the engine treats it exactly as

SteelDesignResultSet.description:
Which design engine produced the results, for one and the same result type

Possible values:

  • 0 - Standard: The standard steel design engine. Native: eResultSetTypeStandard.
  • 1 - AdvancedStability: The non-linear FEM engine ("Advanced stability"). Native: eResultSetTypeMetalNonLinearFEM.
  • 2 - ColdFormed: The cold-formed engine, EN 1993-1-3. Native: eResultSetTypeCFD.

SteelEurocodeAnnex.description:
National annex of Eurocode 3. Mirrors the native `eMetalEurocodeType`. Accepted only together with AD.API.SteelDesignCode`eurocode`, and never with the value `italy` - Italy is a steel standard here (`ntc2008` / `ntc2018`), not an annex.

Possible values:

  • 0 - france: France.
  • 1 - romania: Romania.
  • 2 - general: The general Eurocode annex - no national deviations. Native
  • 3 - uk: United Kingdom.
  • 4 - germany: Germany.
  • 5 - czech: Czech Republic.
  • 6 - italy: Italy. NOT writable: Italy is a steel standard here, not an annex. Reported by GetEnvironment when a model carries it.
  • 7 - poland: Poland.
  • 8 - slovakia: Slovakia.
  • 9 - spain: Spain.
  • 10 - portugal: Portugal.

SteelExecutionClass.description:
EN 1090-2 execution class

Possible values:

  • 0 - exc1: EXC1 - lowest consequence of failure, static loading only.
  • 1 - exc2: EXC2 - the usual execution class for ordinary building structures. Default.
  • 2 - exc3: EXC3 - higher consequence of failure or fatigue loading.
  • 3 - exc4: EXC4 - highest consequence of failure.
  • 4 - not_set: No execution class selected.

SteelExecutionClassType.description:
Whether the EN 1090-2 execution class is global or imposed on the template

Possible values:

  • 0 - global_execution_class: The execution class is taken from the model-wide (global) setting; the per-template value is ignored.
  • 1 - imposed_execution_class: The execution class is imposed on this template, through EC3SteelLinearDesignTemplate.ExecutionClassValue.

SteelFamilyOfElement.description:
Family of element used for the execution-class determination

Possible values:

  • 0 - family_n: Family N - elements not covered by the other families.
  • 1 - family_a: Family A - secondary elements of a simple structure.
  • 2 - family_b: Family B - secondary elements.
  • 3 - family_c: Family C - main elements of a simple structure.
  • 4 - family_d: Family D - main elements.
  • 5 - family_d_plus: Family D+ - main elements with increased requirements.
  • 6 - family_e: Family E - common main structure elements. Default.
  • 7 - family_e_plus: Family E+ - common main structure elements with increased requirements.

SteelFireEmissivityCoeffType.description:
Surface emissivity of the steel member

Possible values:

  • 0 - carbon_steel: Emissivity of plain carbon steel (0.7 per EN 1993-1-2). Default.
  • 1 - hot_dip_galvanised: Emissivity of hot-dip galvanised steel.
  • 2 - imposed: The emissivity is imposed by the user. This is the only value for which the companion emissivity value property is editable.

SteelFireExposedFaces.description:
Number of faces of the cross-section exposed to the fire

Possible values:

  • 0 - four_faces: All four faces of the cross-section are exposed to the fire. Default.
  • 1 - three_faces: Three faces are exposed; the fourth is protected, typically by a slab.

SteelFireProtectionMode.description:
Shape of the fire-protection material around the section

Possible values:

  • 0 - contour_encasement: Contour encasement: the protection follows the profile of the cross-section. Default.
  • 1 - hollow_encasement: Hollow encasement: the protection forms a box around the cross-section.

columnImperfections.description:
Sway and bow imperfections applied to columns (maps to
"RoleColumnSwayImperfections"). 

Send null to leave the whole group unchanged on Update. 

Default value : null

beamImperfections.description:
Bow imperfections applied to beams (maps to "RoleBeamSwayImperfections"). 

Send null to leave the whole group unchanged on Update. 

Default value : null

e0Ly.description:
Relative local bow imperfection e0/L about the y axis (maps to "e0Ly"). 

STORED BUT INERT - it round-trips faithfully and influences nothing. e0/L is a RESULT in
Advance Design, not an input: the steel design run computes it and writes it on the ELEMENT,
under the different names "e0LColumnY" / "e0LColumnZ" / "e0LBeam", from where the report reads
it back. No dialog, accessor or solver ever reads this design-template field, and because the
element uses other names `ApplyRole` cannot propagate it either. It is kept in the
contract so a GET-then-PUT round trip preserves whatever a model already holds; do not expect
setting it to change a design. 

Unit : adimensional 

Default value : 0.0

e0Lz.description:
Relative local bow imperfection e0/L about the z axis (maps to "e0Lz"). 

STORED BUT INERT - it round-trips faithfully and influences nothing. e0/L is a RESULT in
Advance Design, not an input: the steel design run computes it and writes it on the ELEMENT,
under the different names "e0LColumnY" / "e0LColumnZ" / "e0LBeam", from where the report reads
it back. No dialog, accessor or solver ever reads this design-template field, and because the
element uses other names `ApplyRole` cannot propagate it either. It is kept in the
contract so a GET-then-PUT round trip preserves whatever a model already holds; do not expect
setting it to change a design. 

Unit : adimensional 

Default value : 0.0

SteelGlobalSwayImperfections.description:
"Global sway imperfections" group of an EC3 steel design template (maps to the AD model object
`som.RoleSDGlobalSwayImperfections`). 


EC3 only: Advance Design creates this group only when the model is configured for the Eurocode
(1st or 2nd generation). It holds the equivalent geometric imperfections of EN 1993-1-1
clause 5.3, split between a column set and a beam set.

SteelHssDesignThickness.description:
Fraction of the nominal wall thickness used as the HSS design thickness

Possible values:

  • 0 - reduced: The reduced design thickness of the active code: 0.93 x nominal under AISC, 0.90 x nominal under CAN/CSA. Default.
  • 1 - nominal: The full nominal wall thickness (factor 1.00), for HSS whose manufacturing process does not call for the reduction.

SteelImperfectionForceDirectionPivot.description:
How the direction of the imperfection forces is oriented on a super-element

Possible values:

  • 0 - none: No pivot is used to orient the imperfection forces. Default.
  • 1 - use_points: The direction is derived from the geometry, using the points of the super-element.
  • 2 - use_dof_results: The direction is derived from the degree-of-freedom results of a previous analysis.

SteelInitialDeformationShape.description:
Shape of the initial deformation of the non-linear analysis

Possible values:

  • 0 - dominant_eigen_shape: The initial deformation follows the dominant eigen shape of the buckling analysis. Default.
  • 1 - parabolic_variation: The initial deformation follows a parabolic variation defined segment by segment.

elementVerification.description:
Whether the buckling of the element is verified (maps to "BucklingChecking"). 

Displayed as "Elem. Verification". When false, the whole AD.API.SteelLinearBuckling.BucklingLength group is
ignored by the design engine. 

Default value : true

bucklingLength.description:
Buckling lengths and their determination modes (maps to "RoleSteelBucklingLength"). 

Send null to leave the whole group unchanged on Update. 

Default value : null

SteelLinearBuckling.description:
"Buckling" group of a steel design template (maps to the AD model object
`som.RoleSDLinearBuckling`). Holds the flexural and torsional buckling verification.

elementVerification.description:
Whether the deflection of the element is verified (maps to "DeflectionChecking"). 

Displayed as "Elem. Verification". When false, the whole AD.API.SteelLinearDeflection.Deflections group is
ignored by the design engine. 

Default value : true

deflections.description:
Deflection limits applied to the element (maps to "RoleDeflection"). 

Send null to leave the whole group unchanged on Update. 

Default value : null

superElementVerification.description:
Whether the deflection of the super-element is verified (maps to
"SuperElementDeflectionChecking"). 

Displayed as "Super Elem. Verification". When false, the whole
AD.API.SteelLinearDeflection.SuperElementDeflections group is ignored by the design engine. 

Default value : false

superElementDeflections.description:
Deflection limits applied to the super-element (maps to "RoleSuperElementDeflection"). 

Send null to leave the whole group unchanged on Update. 

Default value : null

SteelLinearDeflection.description:
"Deflections" group of a steel design template (maps to the AD model object
`som.RoleSDLinearDeflection`). Holds the serviceability deflection checks, both for the
element itself and for the super-element it belongs to.

SteelLinearDesignResultType.description:
Family of steel design results to extract for a linear element

Possible values:

  • 0 - All: Every result family available for the element under the model's active design code. Families the element has no results for are simply absent from the response rather than reported as an error.
  • 1 - Deflection1: Deflections checked against the first allowable-deflection criterion. Available under every steel design code. Native: SRT_Deflections1.
  • 2 - Deflection2: Deflections checked against the second allowable-deflection criterion. Available under every steel design code. Native: SRT_Deflections2.
  • 3 - BucklingLengths: Flexural buckling lengths and the corresponding slendernesses. Available under every steel design code. Native: SRT_Buckling.
  • 4 - LateralTorsionalBucklingLengths: Lateral-torsional buckling lengths and the corresponding slendernesses, plus - under a Eurocode only - the EN 1993-1-6 shell buckling data of class 4 circular hollow sections. Native: SRT_LBuckling.
  • 5 - Stability: Member stability - flexural and lateral-torsional buckling reduction factors, interaction factors and the combined bending-and-axial-compression checks. EUROCODE 3 ONLY. Native: SRT_Stability.
  • 6 - CrossSectionResistance: Cross-section resistance checks. Available under every steel design code. Native: SRT_Resistance.
  • 7 - FireResistance: Resistance and stability in the fire design situation. EUROCODE 3 ONLY - Advance Design runs no fire design under AISC 360 or CSA S16, so no result set exists to read. Native: SRT_FireResistance.
  • 8 - AdvancedStabilityResistance: Stress-based checks and the critical load factor from the non-linear FEM engine. Requesting this implies the AdvancedStability result set. EUROCODE 3 ONLY - Steel_ResistanceFactory has no eResultSetTypeMetalNonLinearFEM branch for the North American codes. Native: SRT_ResistanceNonLinearMetalFEM.
  • 9 - MaxWorkRatio: The governing work ratio per element, and the per-family maxima it was taken from. Available for Eurocode 3 1st generation and for the North American codes. Native: SRT_MaxWorkRatio.
  • 10 - CrossSectionClass: Cross-section classification, per loading pattern, with the per-plate detail. Available under every steel design code. No native SRT_* value; served by CGrResultManager::GetSteelClass().
  • 11 - FireCrossSectionClass: Cross-section classification in the fire design situation. EUROCODE 3 ONLY - see
  • 12 - FireTemperature: Steel and critical temperatures reached in the fire design situation. EUROCODE 3 ONLY - see
  • 13 - WebShearBuckling: Web shear buckling to EN 1993-1-5. No native SRT_* value; served by CGrResultManager::GetSteelResistanceShearBuckling(). Available for Eurocode 3 only.
  • 14 - CrossSectionInfo: The cross-section the element was verified with - its dimensions and its section properties. Available for EN 1993 2ND GENERATION and for the NORTH AMERICAN codes; the 1st generation has no equivalent family. No native SRT_* value.
  • 15 - ColdFormedResistance: Cold-formed cross-section resistance, clause by clause - EN 1993-1-3 under a Eurocode and AISI S100 / CSA S136 under a North American code. Implies the ColdFormed result set. Native: SRT_Resistance with eResultSetTypeCFD.
  • 16 - ColdFormedDeflection1: Cold-formed deflections against the first criterion. Implies the ColdFormed result set. Available under every steel design code. Native: SRT_Deflections1 with eResultSetTypeCFD.
  • 17 - ColdFormedDeflection2: Cold-formed deflections against the second criterion. Implies the ColdFormed result set. Available under every steel design code. Native: SRT_Deflections2 with eResultSetTypeCFD.
  • 18 - ColdFormedSectionInfo: Gross and effective cross-section properties, and the material strengths, of a COLD-FORMED element, at its start and at its end. Available under every steel design code, for cold-formed elements only. No native SRT_* value; read through CGrLinearElementEC3CFDSectionInfo (&CM_CFD_ELE_SEC_INFO.bin), the accessor the profile-info report reads it with.
  • 19 - ProfileOptimisation: The section the optimiser proposes for the element, with the work ratios before and after. Available under every steel design code the API serves. No native SRT_* value; read through CGrLinearElementSteelProfileOptimisation (&CM_OPT.bin, &CM_CFD_OPT.bin) and CGrLinearElementAISCProfileOptimisation (&AISC_OPT.bin) - the accessors the steel report reads it with.
  • 20 - HaunchSectionProperties: Section properties of the haunches at the two ends of the element. EUROCODE 3 1ST GENERATION ONLY. No native SRT_* value; read through CGrLinearElementEC3Haunch (&CM_HAU.bin).
  • 21 - BucklingLengthCoefficients: The end-restraint coefficients the automatic buckling-length computation derived, and the finite element nodes they belong to. EUROCODE 3 ONLY, both generations. No native SRT_* value; read through CGrLinearElementEta1Eta2Accessor (&EC3_ETA1ETA2ELEM.bin), the accessor the eta-node report table reads it with.
  • 22 - BucklingLengthNodeRestraints: The nodal restraint topology those coefficients were derived from - which members frame into each end of the element, and how much each group contributes. EUROCODE 3 ONLY, both generations. No native SRT_* value; read through CGrEC3NodeEtaAccessor (&EC3_ETA1ETA2NODEY.bin, &EC3_ETA1ETA2NODEZ.bin), the accessor the eta-by-node report table reads it with.
  • 23 - GlobalSwayImperfectionForces: The equivalent horizontal forces generated for the global sway imperfection of EN 1993-1-1 5.3.2(4), per combination. EUROCODE 3 ONLY, both generations. No native SRT_* value; read through CGrEC3ImperfectionForcesAccessor (&EC3_SwayForces.bin).
  • 24 - LocalBowImperfectionForces: The equivalent forces generated for the local bow imperfection of EN 1993-1-1 5.3.2(3), per combination, for columns and beams alike. EUROCODE 3 ONLY, both generations. No native SRT_* value; read through CGrEC3ImperfectionForcesAccessor (&EC3_BowForces.bin).

designCode.description:
Steel design code the model is configured with, and therefore the code whose expert property
set this template carries. 

Output only: it is read from the model settings, not stored on the template. A value sent on
Create or Update is ignored. 

The Eurocode property set (AD.API.EC3SteelLinearDesignTemplate) is used by
AD.API.SteelDesignCode.eurocode,
AD.API.SteelDesignCode.ntc2008 and AD.API.SteelDesignCode.ntc2018. 

The AISC property set (AD.API.AISCSteelLinearDesignTemplate) is used by
AD.API.SteelDesignCode.aisc and AD.API.SteelDesignCode.aisc_2016. 

The CAN/CSA property set (AD.API.CSASteelLinearDesignTemplate) is used by
AD.API.SteelDesignCode.can_csa_s16_2009, AD.API.SteelDesignCode.can_csa_s16_2014,
AD.API.SteelDesignCode.can_csa_s16_2019 and
AD.API.SteelDesignCode.can_csa_s16_2024. 

Default value : SteelDesignCode.eurocode

SteelLinearDesignTemplate.description:
Base class of the Expert design templates that apply to linear STEEL elements - the templates
whose AD.API.DesignTemplate.MaterialType is
AD.API.DesignTemplateMaterialType.steel. 


The steel design properties themselves depend on the steel design code configured on the model,
so they live on the per-code leaf classes. Two families are exposed: 

- the EUROCODE family, AD.API.EC3SteelLinearDesignTemplate, 

- the NORTH-AMERICAN family, AD.API.NorthAmericanSteelLinearDesignTemplate and its two
  leaves AD.API.AISCSteelLinearDesignTemplate and
  AD.API.CSASteelLinearDesignTemplate. 


IMPORTANT - the design code is a MODEL-WIDE setting, not a per-template one. When a template is
created, Advance Design allocates the expert property set of the code the model is configured
with, and only that one. Sending a leaf that does not match the active code is therefore
refused, with the active code reported in the response diagnostics: an
AD.API.EC3SteelLinearDesignTemplate needs a Eurocode model, an
AD.API.AISCSteelLinearDesignTemplate an AISC one and a
AD.API.CSASteelLinearDesignTemplate a CAN/CSA one. 

Available for the descriptive model only.

SteelLocalBowImperfectionEffect.description:
Verification the local bow imperfection is applied to

Possible values:

  • 0 - flexural_buckling: The local bow imperfection is applied for flexural buckling, EN 1993-1-1 equation (7.9). Default for columns.
  • 1 - lateral_torsional_buckling: The local bow imperfection is applied for lateral-torsional buckling, EN 1993-1-1 equation (7.11). Default for beams.
  • 2 - max_of_buckling_and_ltb: The most unfavourable of the flexural-buckling and lateral-torsional-buckling imperfections is retained.

SteelLtbCriticalMomentMode.description:
How the elastic critical moment Mcr is obtained

Possible values:

  • 0 - auto_mcr: Mcr is computed by the design engine from the section, the lateral-torsional buckling length and the C1..C3 coefficients. Default.
  • 1 - imposed_mcr: Mcr is taken from the value the caller imposes.
  • 2 - from_advanced_stability: Mcr is taken from the "Advance stability (2nd order)" non-linear finite-element analysis rather than from a closed-form expression, so the imposed value is NOT used. Restricted: Advance Design accepts this only for a cold-formed section under the 2nd-generation Eurocode, and silently resets it to auto_mcr on an element whose section is not cold-formed.

SteelLtbCurveMethod.description:
Method used for the lateral-torsional-buckling reduction factor

Possible values:

  • 0 - general_case: General case: EN 1993-1-1 clause 6.3.2.2 under the 1st-generation Eurocode, clause 8.3.2.3(2) under the 2nd generation. The only ordinal that means the same thing in both generations.
  • 1 - rolled_welded_profiles: Rolled or equivalent welded profiles, EN 1993-1-1 clause 6.3.2.3, under the 1st-generation Eurocode; under the 2nd generation this same ordinal means doubly-symmetric I and H sections, clause 8.3.2.4(3), instead.
  • 2 - least_favorable: The least favourable of the two methods above is retained, under the 1st-generation Eurocode; under the 2nd generation this same ordinal means buckling of the compression flange, clause 8.3.2.4, and NOT the least favourable method. Either way this is the value Advance Design stores in a newly created template, whatever the Eurocode generation, which is why a 2nd-generation template starts out on the buckling of the compression flange.
  • 3 - most_favorable: The most favourable of the two methods above is retained, under the 1st-generation Eurocode; under the 2nd generation this same ordinal means the least favourable is retained, which is the 2nd generation's own default and NOT the most favourable method.
  • 4 - second_generation_most_favorable: 2nd-generation Eurocode ONLY: the most favourable of the methods above is retained. The 1st-generation option list has no such ordinal, and the engine falls back on the least favourable method when it reads this value under the 1st generation, so send it only when the model runs the 2nd-generation Eurocode.

SteelLtbEndRestraint.description:
Lateral restraint at one end of a lateral-torsional-buckling span

Possible values:

  • 0 - no_restraint: No lateral restraint at this end.
  • 1 - pinned: Pinned (articulated) lateral restraint at this end: lateral displacement is prevented but the section is free to rotate. Default.
  • 2 - fixed: Fixed (clamped) lateral restraint at this end: both lateral displacement and rotation are prevented.

SteelLtbFCoefficientMode.description:
How the f correction coefficient is obtained

Possible values:

  • 0 - auto_coefficient: The f coefficient is computed automatically by the design engine.
  • 1 - none: No f correction is applied (f = 1.0). Default.
  • 2 - imposed_kc: The correction factor kc is imposed by the user through the companion value property; f is derived from it.
  • 3 - imposed_f: The f coefficient itself is imposed by the user through the companion value property.

SteelLtbFactorCbMode.description:
How the Cb moment modification factor is obtained (North-American codes)

Possible values:

  • 0 - auto_cb: Cb is computed automatically by the design engine from the moment diagram of the lateral-torsional-buckling span. Default.
  • 1 - imposed_cb: Cb is imposed by the user through the companion value property.

SteelLtbFactorFMMode.description:
How the fM factor is obtained

Possible values:

  • 0 - auto_factor: The fM factor is computed automatically by the design engine. Default.
  • 1 - value_1: The fM factor is forced to 1.0.
  • 2 - user_defined: The fM factor is imposed by the user through the companion value property.

SteelLtbIntermediateRestraintType.description:
Nature of the intermediate lateral restraints

Possible values:

  • 0 - pinned: The intermediate restraints are pinned: lateral displacement is prevented but the section is free to rotate. Default.
  • 1 - fixed: The intermediate restraints are fixed: both lateral displacement and rotation are prevented.

SteelLtbLoadApplicationPoint.description:
Point of application of the transverse load

Possible values:

  • 0 - neutral_fiber: The load is applied at the neutral fibre of the cross-section. Default (except under the British national annex, which defaults to destabilising).
  • 1 - upper_fiber: The load is applied at the upper fibre of the cross-section.
  • 2 - lower_fiber: The load is applied at the lower fibre of the cross-section.
  • 3 - destabilising: The load is treated as destabilising, i.e. it is free to move sideways with the section.
  • 4 - stabilising: The load is treated as stabilising.
  • 5 - imposed_value: The point of application is imposed by the user through the companion zg / zj values.

SteelLtbLoadType.description:
Loading pattern used to pick the C1 / C2 / C3 coefficients

Possible values:

  • 0 - auto_load_type: The loading pattern is recognised automatically by the design engine from the internal forces diagram. Default.
  • 1 - column: Column: the element carries end moments only, no transverse load.
  • 2 - simple_beam_with_uniform_loads: Simply supported beam carrying uniformly distributed loads.
  • 3 - fixed_beam_with_uniform_loads: Beam fixed at both ends carrying uniformly distributed loads.
  • 4 - simple_beam_with_point_load: Simply supported beam carrying a concentrated load.
  • 5 - fixed_beam_with_point_load: Beam fixed at both ends carrying a concentrated load.
  • 6 - another_case: Any other loading pattern; the coefficients are then taken from the imposed C1 / C2 / C3 values.

SteelLtbReferenceCriticalMomentMode.description:
How the reference elastic critical moment Mcr,0 is obtained

Possible values:

  • 0 - auto_mcr0: Mcr,0 is computed by the design engine. Default.
  • 1 - imposed_mcr0: Mcr,0 is taken from the value the caller imposes.
  • 2 - same_as_mcr: Mcr,0 reuses whatever Mcr resolves to, so the imposed Mcr,0 value is NOT used.

SteelLtbRestraintDefinitionType.description:
How the intermediate lateral restraints are positioned

Possible values:

  • 0 - by_number: The intermediate restraints are defined by their count: they are distributed evenly along the span. RestraintDefinitionValues holds the number of restraints.
  • 1 - by_abscissa: The intermediate restraints are defined by their absolute abscissa along the element, in metres. RestraintDefinitionValues holds the list of abscissae.
  • 2 - by_ratio: The intermediate restraints are defined by their relative position along the element, as a ratio in the range 0..1. RestraintDefinitionValues holds the list of ratios.

SteelManufacturingQuality.description:
EN 1993-1-6 fabrication tolerance quality class

Possible values:

  • 0 - class_a: Fabrication tolerance quality class A ("Excellent"), Q = 40 in EN 1993-1-6.
  • 1 - class_b: Fabrication tolerance quality class B ("High"), Q = 25 in EN 1993-1-6.
  • 2 - class_c: Fabrication tolerance quality class C ("Normal"), Q = 16 in EN 1993-1-6. Default.

SteelMaxWorkRatioComponent.description:
The governing work ratio of an element and the per-family maxima behind it

Possible values:

  • 0 - Overall: Governing work ratio across every family. Native: MaxWorkRatio_MAX.
  • 1 - Deflections: Maximum work ratio of the deflection checks. Native: MaxWorkRatio_Deflections.
  • 2 - CrossSectionResistance: Maximum work ratio of the cross-section resistance checks. Native: MaxWorkRatio_Resistance.
  • 3 - Stability: Maximum work ratio of the member stability checks. Native: MaxWorkRatio_Stability.
  • 4 - FireResistance: Maximum work ratio of the fire resistance checks. Native: MaxWorkRatio_FireResistance.
  • 5 - FireStability: Maximum work ratio of the fire stability checks. Native: MaxWorkRatio_FireStability.

runNonLinearFEM.description:
Whether the non-linear 2nd-order analysis with warping and imperfections is run (maps to
"MetalRunNonLinearFEM"). 

Displayed as "2nd order with warping and imperfections". When false, every other property of
this group is read-only in Advance Design and ignored by the design engine. 

Default value : false

factorForDominantEigenMode.description:
Scale factor applied to the dominant eigen mode used as the initial deformation (maps to
"FactorForDominantEigenMode"). 

Valid range 150..1000. Advance Design does not currently display this property, but it is
stored and propagated. 

Default value : 900

numberOfIterations.description:
Maximum number of iterations of the non-linear solver (maps to "NumberOfIterations"). 

Displayed as "Number of iterations". Valid range 1..100. 

Default value : 10

useForDeflectionChecks.description:
Whether the results of the non-linear analysis are used for the deflection checks (maps to
"UseForDeflectionChecks"). 

Default value : false

annexC2Application.description:
Whether the EN 1993-1-1 annex C.2 approach is applied (maps to "AnexC2Application"). 

2nd-generation Eurocode only: Advance Design hides it for the other steel codes. 

Default value : false

parameters.description:
Detailed parameters of the non-linear analysis (maps to "Parameters"). 

These are the contents of the "Stability - 2nd order parameters" dialog of Advance
Design. 

Send null to leave the whole group unchanged on Update. 

Default value : null

SteelNonLinearFEM.description:
"Advance stability (2nd order)" group of a steel design template (maps to the AD model object
`som.RoleMetalNonLinearFEM`). 


Drives the non-linear (2nd order) finite-element analysis with warping and imperfections that
Advance Design runs in place of the code's simplified stability checks.

SteelNonLinearFEMDofStatus.description:
Status of one degree of freedom of a non-linear FEM punctual support

Possible values:

  • 0 - auto_status: The status is determined automatically by the design engine. Default.
  • 1 - rigid: The degree of freedom is rigidly restrained.
  • 2 - free: The degree of freedom is free.
  • 3 - elastic: The degree of freedom is elastically restrained, with the stiffness given by the companion value property.
  • -1 - indeterminate: Undetermined; used when the value has never been set.

SteelNonLinearFEMDofType.description:
Preset applied to the degrees of freedom of a non-linear FEM punctual support

Possible values:

  • 0 - fully_rigid: All degrees of freedom are rigidly restrained. Default.
  • 1 - auto_dof: The restraints are determined automatically by the design engine.
  • 2 - hinged: Hinged: translations are restrained, rotations are free.
  • 3 - custom: Custom: every degree of freedom is taken from its individual status and value properties.
  • 4 - ty_rx_restraint: Restraint of the lateral translation Ty and of the torsional rotation Rx.
  • 5 - ty_restraint: Restraint of the lateral translation Ty only.
  • 6 - fully_free: All degrees of freedom are free.
  • -1 - indeterminate: Undetermined; used when the value has never been set.

SteelNonLinearFEMLoadsOffset.description:
Point of the cross-section at which the loads are applied

Possible values:

  • 0 - top_left: Loads are applied at the top-left corner of the cross-section.
  • 1 - top_center: Loads are applied at the top-centre of the cross-section.
  • 2 - top_right: Loads are applied at the top-right corner of the cross-section.
  • 3 - center_left: Loads are applied at the centre-left of the cross-section.
  • 4 - center: Loads are applied at the centre of the cross-section. Default.
  • 5 - center_right: Loads are applied at the centre-right of the cross-section.
  • 6 - bottom_left: Loads are applied at the bottom-left corner of the cross-section.
  • 7 - bottom_center: Loads are applied at the bottom-centre of the cross-section.
  • 8 - bottom_right: Loads are applied at the bottom-right corner of the cross-section.
  • 9 - user_defined: Loads are applied at a user-defined point, given by the companion offset y and z values.
  • -1 - indeterminate: Undetermined; used when the value has never been set.

SteelNonLinearFEMOffsetPosition.description:
Position over the section height at which a non-linear FEM support acts

Possible values:

  • 0 - neutral_fiber: The support acts at the neutral fibre of the cross-section. Default.
  • 1 - upper_fiber: The support acts at the upper fibre of the cross-section.
  • 2 - bottom_fiber: The support acts at the bottom fibre of the cross-section.
  • 3 - imposed_value: The support acts at a user-imposed offset, given by the companion offset value property.
  • -1 - indeterminate: Undetermined position; used when the value has never been set.

SteelNonLinearFEMParameters.description:
Detailed parameters of the non-linear (2nd order) analysis (maps to the AD model object
`som.ParametersMetalNonLinearFEM`) - the "Stability - 2nd order parameters" dialog.

mode.description:
What changes together when a section is replaced. `eOptimizationParElements` by default.


`eOptimizationNonExistant` is a sentinel of the shared enumeration and is refused:
nothing ever stores it in a model, and the dialog's radio group cannot be cleared.

optimizeWhenStrengthRatioAbove.description:
Replace the section when the strength / stability work ratio exceeds
AD.API.SteelOptimizationSettings.StrengthRatioUpperLimit. On by default.

strengthRatioUpperLimit.description:
The upper strength / stability work ratio, as a PERCENTAGE. 100 by default. Must stay
above AD.API.SteelOptimizationSettings.StrengthRatioLowerLimit whenever both criteria are enabled.

optimizeWhenStrengthRatioBelow.description:
Replace the section when the strength / stability work ratio falls below
AD.API.SteelOptimizationSettings.StrengthRatioLowerLimit - the over-designed case. Off by default.

strengthRatioLowerLimit.description: The lower strength / stability work ratio, as a PERCENTAGE. 50 by default.

optimizeWhenDeflectionRatioAbove.description:
Replace the section when the max / allowable deflection ratio exceeds
AD.API.SteelOptimizationSettings.DeflectionRatioUpperLimit. On by default under the Eurocode.

deflectionRatioUpperLimit.description: The deflection ratio limit, as a PERCENTAGE. 100 by default.

searchRange.description:
How far the search may go. `eProfileOptimizationSearchRangeAuto` by default, which ignores
AD.API.SteelOptimizationSettings.MaximumIterationCount.

maximumIterationCount.description:
The iteration ceiling, read only when AD.API.SteelOptimizationSettings.SearchRange is
`eProfileOptimizationSearchRangeAutoWithMaxLimit`. Between 1 and 100; 8 by default.

SteelOptimizationSettings.description:
The Optimisation page: when the shape calculation is allowed to replace a section, and how
widely it may search.



Read only by the run that calculates shapes - see
AD.API.SteelCalculationSequenceSettings.CalculateShapes. Shared by both steel code
families; every rule below holds whatever the model's steel code is.



EACH LIMIT FOLLOWS ITS OWN SWITCH. The three thresholds and the iteration ceiling are
separate properties from the switches that enable them, and the dialog greys each edit out
while its switch is off. A value sent without its switch is stored and reported as a
warning, so send the pair together.

sortCriterion.description:
Which work ratio decides that a candidate is acceptable. `eTriCriteriaEnveloppe` by default
under the Eurocode.

orderingCriterion.description: The order candidates are tried in. `ByWeight` by default.

minimumHeight.description: Smallest acceptable section height, in metres. 0.10 by default.

maximumHeight.description: Largest acceptable section height, in metres. 1.00 by default.

minimumWidth.description: Smallest acceptable section width, in metres. 0.10 by default.

maximumWidth.description: Largest acceptable section width, in metres. 1.00 by default.

SteelProfileSortingSettings.description:
The Sort profiles page: the order in which candidate sections are tried, and the size band
they are taken from.



THE FOUR LIMITS ARE IN METRES. They are cross-section dimensions, so they follow the SI
convention of the rest of the API rather than the display unit of the dialog. Each is read
only while its own switch is on, and one sent without its switch is stored and reported.



A minimum is NOT checked against its maximum, deliberately: the dialog does not check it
either, and refusing here would make the API stricter than the desktop application.



Shared by both steel code families. Only CM66 - which no settings group covers - disables
two of the three sort criteria.

SteelSectionClass.description:
Cross-section class of a steel element, Eurocode and CAN/CSA lists

Possible values:

  • 0 - auto_class: The cross-section class is determined automatically by the design engine from the section geometry and the internal forces.
  • 1 - class_1: Class 1 imposed: cross-section can form a plastic hinge with the rotation capacity required for plastic analysis, without reduction of resistance.
  • 2 - class_2: Class 2 imposed: cross-section can develop its plastic moment resistance, but has limited rotation capacity because of local buckling.
  • 3 - class_3: Class 3 imposed: the stress in the extreme compression fibre can reach the yield strength, but local buckling prevents development of the plastic moment resistance.
  • 4 - class_4: Class 4 imposed: local buckling occurs before the yield stress is reached in one or more parts of the cross-section. This is the only class for which the effective characteristics (Sxeff, eNy, eNz, Weff*) can be imposed.

SteelSectionClassAISC.description:
Cross-section class of a steel element, AISC list

Possible values:

  • 0 - auto_class: The cross-section class is determined automatically by the design engine from the section geometry and the internal forces. Default.
  • 1 - compact: Compact imposed (AISC 360 clause B4): the section can develop its full plastic moment and has the flange and web slenderness needed for the rotation capacity.
  • 2 - noncompact: Noncompact imposed: yielding can start in the extreme compression fibre, but local buckling prevents the full plastic moment from developing.
  • 3 - slender_element: Slender-element imposed: local buckling of a compression element occurs before the yield stress is reached.

SteelTorsionalBucklingLengthMode.description:

Possible values:

  • 4 - calculated_from_super_element: Lcr,T is computed from the length of the super-element the element belongs to.

  • 6 - calculated_from_mesh_size: Lcr,T is computed from the finite-element mesh size.

TimberCombinationDesign.description:
Properties applied by the timber design engine to one combination. 

The three groups are stored by AD in a single object (`som.TimberFields`, attached to the
combination as "ExpertFieldTimber"), but they are written independently: sending one group does
not disturb the other two. Because that one object is created as soon as any of the three is
written, its existence says nothing about which verifications are configured - so on read a
group is returned only when its design calculation is listed in
AD.API.Combination.DesignCalculations. 

Each group matches one design calculation and is relevant only when the combination lists it:
AD.API.eCombinationDesignCalculation.TimberDeflections,
AD.API.eCombinationDesignCalculation.TimberProfiles and
AD.API.eCombinationDesignCalculation.TimberFire.

  • 2 - ntc2018: NTC 2018 - the current Italian national application of Eurocode 5.
  • 3 - nds_2018: NDS 2018 - the US national design specification for wood construction.
  • 4 - o86_2019: CSA O86-19 - the Canadian timber standard. The timber code of

profileType.description:
Which standard profile shape this section behaves like. Steel design engines use it to pick
the applicable formulae and classification rules; left as Unknown, most code checks are
skipped.

Model key: SECTION_KEY_USER_SECT_PROFILE_TYPE ("UserSectionProfileType")

rollingType.description:
How the section was manufactured (lamination type), which drives the buckling curve
selection. Advance Design assigns Welded to every user section created through its own
interface.

Default value: SectionRollingType_API.Welded

shape.description:
The outline of the section - what the application and its cross-section editor (Sec.exe)
call the "epure". It is the geometry the section is drawn with; it does not change any
sectional characteristic, which is why the characteristics above must be supplied whether an
outline is given or not.

Left null, the section keeps the default outline that Advance Design gives a new user
section: a 50 x 50 mm square centred on the origin. Supplied, it replaces that outline
entirely - see AD.API.UserSectionShape for how to describe a section made of several
areas, or one with holes.

Default value: null (the default square outline is kept)

UserSection.description:
A cross-section whose sectional characteristics are supplied by the caller instead of being
derived from a catalog entry or from parametric dimensions - the equivalent of the "User" tab
of the Advance Design cross-section manager.
            

All values are in SI units (m², m³, m⁴, m⁶), like the rest of the API. Advance Design
never recomputes them for a user section, so every parameter that the analysis or a design
check needs must be provided; the derived quantities (radii of gyration, principal inertias,
principal axis angle, perimeter) are not stored and are not part of this object, exactly as
when the values are typed in the application.
Axis convention: y and z are the section local axes with z positive, the same naming the
application shows. The Advance Design "Z negative" global axis setting does not apply here -
through the API, "Inf" always means the lower fibre.
Every value has to be a finite number: "NaN" and "Infinity" are valid JSON for this
service - the design results carry genuine infinities - but a section built on one would poison
the stiffness matrix, so they are refused. AD.API.UserSection.ProfileType and
AD.API.UserSection.RollingType have to name a value of their enumeration; an integer that names
nothing is refused rather than stored on the section.
On create, AD.API.Section.Type is forced to SectionType_API.st_USER, and
AD.API.Section.FamilyCode ("USECT") and AD.API.Section.CatalogName (empty, the
section only lives in the model) are outputs: any value sent for them is ignored. The user
section catalog database is never modified.

type.description:
Whether this contour is a polygon (a list of vertices) or a circle (a centre and a radius).

Default value: UserSectionContourType_API.Polygon

isHole.description:
False when the contour adds material, true when it removes it - use a hole to describe a
tube, a box or any cell inside another contour. A hole is expected to lie inside a material
contour, and an outline must contain at least one material contour.

Default value: false

points.description:
For a AD.API.UserSectionContourType_API.Polygon: its vertices, listed once in order
around the contour. The contour is closed automatically from the last point back to the
first, so the first point must not be repeated at the end, and no two consecutive points may
coincide. At least three vertices are required. The order is stored exactly as given;
Advance Design writes its own outlines clockwise in the (y, z) plane.

For a AD.API.UserSectionContourType_API.Circle: exactly one point, its centre.

radius.description:
Radius of a AD.API.UserSectionContourType_API.Circle contour, which must be strictly
positive. Ignored on a polygon.

Unit: m

Default value: 0

UserSectionContour.description:
One closed contour of the outline of a user section: either a polygon or a circle, adding
material or removing it. See AD.API.UserSectionShape for how contours combine.

y.description:
Coordinate along the section local y axis - the horizontal axis of the cross-section, with
the origin on the centre of gravity of the section. See AD.API.UserSectionShape for
the axis and origin conventions.

Unit: m

Default value: 0

z.description:
Coordinate along the section local z axis - the vertical axis of the cross-section, positive
upwards, with the origin on the centre of gravity of the section. The fibre at the lowest z
is the one AD.API.UserSection.WelyInf refers to, the fibre at the highest z the one
AD.API.UserSection.WelySup refers to.

Unit: m

Default value: 0

filletRadius.description:
Radius of the fillet (rounding) that replaces the sharp corner at this vertex; 0 keeps the
corner sharp. Use it to describe the root fillets of a rolled profile. Only meaningful on a
AD.API.UserSectionContourType_API.Polygon contour - it is ignored on a circle, whose
radius is AD.API.UserSectionContour.Radius.

The fillet must fit in the corner: its tangent length, radius / tan(angle / 2) where
angle is the interior angle at this vertex, has to stay shorter than both adjacent edges. A
fillet that does not fit is rejected, because Advance Design would draw a corrupted outline
instead of reporting the problem. A fillet on a vertex that does not form a corner - one
sitting on a straight edge between its neighbours - is accepted but has no effect, and is
reported as a warning.
Unit: m

Default value: 0

contours.description:
The contours the outline is made of, at least one of which must add material. Contours are
stored and drawn in the order given.

UserSectionShape.description: The outline of a user section - what Advance Design and its cross-section editor (Sec.exe) call the "epure". It is the geometry the section is drawn with, and what the application derives the bounding box and the section shape from. How to define an outline 1. The points are 2D, in the section local axes, in metres. Every point is a (AD.API.UserSectionContourPoint.Y, AD.API.UserSectionContourPoint.Z) pair in the plane of the cross-section: y is the horizontal axis, z the vertical one and positive upwards. There is no third coordinate - the outline is the constant cross-section of the member, which Advance Design extrudes along its length. 2. The origin is the centre of gravity of the section. Advance Design does not compute the centre of gravity of a user section from its outline: it reports it as (0, 0), and takes that as the reference point when it maps the offsets of the members the section is assigned to. So place the outline with its centroid on the origin. That is also what the application does to the outlines it produces itself - after computing the sectional characteristics it translates the outline so the computed centroid falls on (0, 0). Nothing recentres an outline that arrives through the API: an off-centre outline is stored and drawn exactly where it was put, and the member then looks shifted with respect to its own axis. 3. Which way up matters for an asymmetric section. The elastic section moduli of AD.API.UserSection use the same axes: `WelyInf` and `WelzInf` belong to the fibres at the lowest z and y, `WelySup` and `WelzSup` to those at the highest. Drawing the flange of a T at positive z therefore means "Sup" is the flange side; the characteristics supplied for the section have to agree with the outline. 4. A contour is closed automatically. List the vertices of a polygon once, in order around the contour, and do not repeat the first point at the end. A repeated point leaves a zero length edge and is rejected. A vertex may carry a AD.API.UserSectionContourPoint.FilletRadius to round its corner. 5. Several contours describe several areas. A section made of disjoint parts needs one material contour per part - a double angle is two contours, a double channel is two, a battened box of four angles is four. There is nothing else to declare: the parts do not have to touch, and they are not merged. 6. A hole removes material. Set AD.API.UserSectionContour.IsHole on a contour lying inside a material contour to describe a tube, a box or a cell. Holes and material contours can be mixed freely, in any order, and either kind can be a polygon or a circle - a circular tube is one circle plus one circular hole. 7. The outline is geometry only. Advance Design never derives the sectional characteristics from it, so AD.API.UserSection.Area and every other characteristic still have to be supplied, and they are never checked against the outline. Leaving AD.API.UserSection.Shape null keeps the default outline, a 50 x 50 mm square centred on the origin. Example - a 200 x 100 mm rectangular tube with a 10 mm wall: one rectangle of material and one rectangular hole, both centred on the origin. ``` var tube = new UserSectionShape { Contours = new List { new UserSectionContour // the outside, clockwise { Points = new List { new UserSectionContourPoint { Y = -0.050, Z = 0.100 }, new UserSectionContourPoint { Y = 0.050, Z = 0.100 }, new UserSectionContourPoint { Y = 0.050, Z = -0.100 }, new UserSectionContourPoint { Y = -0.050, Z = -0.100 }, } }, new UserSectionContour // the cell, 10 mm inside it { IsHole = true, Points = new List { new UserSectionContourPoint { Y = -0.040, Z = 0.090 }, new UserSectionContourPoint { Y = 0.040, Z = 0.090 }, new UserSectionContourPoint { Y = 0.040, Z = -0.090 }, new UserSectionContourPoint { Y = -0.040, Z = -0.090 }, } }, } }; ``` Every coordinate, every fillet radius and every circle radius has to be a finite number. "NaN" and "Infinity" are valid JSON for this service, so an outline can be handed one; it is refused rather than drawn. Limitations. A user section that was edited in the cross-section editor (Sec.exe) can carry thin-walled contours in addition to its drawn geometry, which feed the profile segmentation the Advanced Stability solver uses. This object cannot express them: reading such a section returns only its drawn contours, and supplying an outline for it drops the rest, which is reported as a warning. Advance Design also draws two contour kinds this object has no equivalent for - an arc and a segment - and a polyline, whose points carry a camber instead of a fillet radius. Reading a section that uses them reports those contours as polygons, which is exact for a straight polyline (that is what the default square is) but only an approximation for the rest; the read raises a warning naming the section, and such an outline must not be sent back unchanged.

eAnalysisModelState.description:

Possible values:

  • 0 - NotCreated: The project has no analysis model at all: LaunchAnalysis was never run on it and it was not opened from a project file that carried one. Every other property of the status is at its default and says nothing.
  • 1 - Created: An analysis model exists but carries neither a mesh nor results. This is also what is reported in the one case where nothing more could be read: an analysis model that is not open in the session, which a status read must not open. A warning in the response diagnostics says so when that happens - it takes a project the desktop application left in that state, since LaunchAnalysis and OpenProject both leave the model open.
  • 2 - Meshed: The analysis model carries a mesh (complete or incomplete - see MeshState) but no finite element results.
  • 3 - Calculated: The finite element analysis has been run and its results are current as far as the model can tell. Whether any DESIGN expert has run is a separate question, answered per family by AnalysisModelStatus.Design.
  • 4 - OutOfDate: Finite element results exist but the model has been changed since they were produced, so they no longer describe it.

eCombinationsStandard.description:
The combination standard the model generates for - mirrors REG_COMBINATIONS_CODE_*. It defaults to what the session localization (`Environments.Localization`) resolves to, the same way the desktop application resolves it from its installation: US and Asia give `US`, Canada gives `CanadaCNB2020`, Italy gives `NTC2018`, every other localization gives `Eurocode`. TO CHOOSE IT, set `Environments.DesignCodes.Combinations` on the `NewProject` or `OpenProject` call. It is a SESSION setting and cannot be changed afterwards, so it is still read only where it appears on the settings themselves: setting `CombinationsGenerationSettings.Standard` in a `SetModelSettings` request is ignored. The 2nd generation Eurocode (EN 1990:2023) is not in this list at all: it is not released, so it cannot be asked for and cannot be named in a response. A model that already generates to it - one configured that way by the desktop application - is REFUSED by the settings operations and by `GenerateCombinations`, on every installation that does not have that standard enabled. Answering it under EN 1990:2002 instead would be a wrong answer that looks like a right one.

Possible values:

  • 0 - Eurocode: EN 1990 (1st generation), with the national annex of the localization.
  • 1 - US: ASCE / AISC / ACI, pre-2018 edition.
  • 2 - Canada: Canada NBC 2010.
  • 3 - EurocodeItalia: Eurocode with the older Italian coefficients (NTC 2008).
  • 4 - CanadaNBC2015: Canada NBC 2015.
  • 5 - NTC2018: Italy NTC 2018. Shares the Eurocode settings, with GEO active.
  • 6 - Greenhouse_EN13031_1: PR EN 13031-1 - greenhouses.
  • 7 - US2018: ASCE / AISC / ACI, 2018 edition.
  • 8 - CanadaCNB2020: Canada CNB 2020.

eConcreteCombinationType.description:
Limit state under which the concrete design engine checks a combination.

Possible values:

  • 0 - Uls: Ultimate limit state (ELU). Default for combinations whose project situation is ULS.
  • 1 - UlsAccidental: Accidental ultimate limit state (ELU accidentelle). Default for combinations whose project situation is ULS accidental or SLS accidental.
  • 2 - Sls: Serviceability limit state (ELS). Default for combinations whose project situation is SLS.
  • 3 - None: The combination is not checked under any limit state by the concrete design engine.

eConcreteLoadDuration.description:
Load duration used by the concrete design engine for a combination.

Possible values:

  • 0 - ShortTerm: Short duration, under 1 hour. Default for accidental combinations.
  • 1 - MediumTerm: Medium duration, between 1 and 24 hours.
  • 2 - LongTerm: Long duration, over 24 hours. Default for non-accidental combinations.
  • 3 - None: No duration assigned.

eDeflectionCriterion.description:

Possible values:

  • 0 - FirstCriterion: First deflection criterion. Labelled "Wmax" under the 2nd generation Eurocode. Default.
  • 1 - SecondCriterion: Second deflection criterion. Labelled "W3" under the 2nd generation Eurocode.
  • 2 - BothCriteria: Both criteria are checked. Available under EC3 only - under any other steel design code the engine reads this value as "no criterion".
  • 3 - None: No deflection criterion is checked. Under a design code other than EC3 use

eDesignVerificationState.description:
Whether a verification is evaluated for a combination listed for it.

Possible values:

  • 0 - Active: The verification is evaluated for this combination. Default.
  • 1 - Inactive: The verification is skipped for this combination, although the combination stays in its list and keeps its coefficients.

eEurocodeCombinationEquation.description:
Which ULS equation of EN 1990 the fundamental combinations are built with. Offered by the General, Poland, Czech and Slovakia annexes only; elsewhere the annex fixes it and the value is not read.

Possible values:

  • 0 - Equation_6_10: Equation 6.10 - one combination per leading variable action.
  • 1 - Equation_6_10a_6_10b: Equations 6.10a and 6.10b - the reduced permanent action alternative.

eExploitationCategory.description:
Live load (exploitation) category of EN 1991-1-1, which fixes psi0 / psi1 / psi2 - mirrors enumExploitationSituation. IMPORTANT - the list is annex dependent, because som.ModelProperties stores a plain index into that annex's own list. The enumerators below are the GENERAL list, which the UK, German, Polish, Romanian and Slovakian annexes share. Two annexes differ: - France has thirteen categories, indexed A, B, C, D, E1, E2a, E2b, E2c, F, G, H, K, K1, then 13 = user defined. Index 4 therefore means E1 there, not `CategoryE`. - The Czech annex stops at H, so 8 = user defined and `CategoryI` / `CategoryJ` do not exist. A value the active annex does not have is refused rather than silently accepted.

Possible values:

  • 0 - CategoryA: A - domestic and residential areas.
  • 1 - CategoryB: B - office areas.
  • 2 - CategoryC: C - congregation areas.
  • 3 - CategoryD: D - shopping areas.
  • 4 - CategoryE: E - storage areas.
  • 5 - CategoryF: F - traffic areas, vehicle weight under 30 kN.
  • 6 - CategoryG: G - traffic areas, vehicle weight 30 to 160 kN.
  • 7 - CategoryH: H - roofs.
  • 8 - CategoryI: I - soil settlements (German annex).
  • 9 - CategoryJ: J - other impacts (German annex).
  • 10 - UserDefined: psi0 / psi1 / psi2 are used as they are sent instead of being taken from the annex's table. The only category in which they are writable.

eGreenhouseConsequenceClass.description:

  • 2 - C2:
  • 3 - Other: Neither class: the consequence factors on the settings are used as they are sent.
